# # Build an HMM from a multiple sequence alignment

import pyhmmer
pyhmmer.__version__

alphabet = pyhmmer.easel.Alphabet.amino()

# ## Loading the alignment

# A new HMM can be built from a single sequence, or from a multiple sequence alignment. Let's load an alignment in digital mode so that we can build our HMM. We can use a `MSAFile` to read an alignment from a file in one of the supported formats (such as [Stockholm](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-stockholm), [Clustal](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-clustal), [aligned FASTA](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-fasta), *etc*; see the `MSAFile` documentation for the complete list):

with pyhmmer.easel.MSAFile("data/msa/LuxC.sto", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as msa_file:
    msa = msa_file.read()

# <div class="alert alert-info">
#
# Note
#     
# In this example, we load a multiple sequence alignment from a file, but if your program produces alignment and you wish to make an HMM out of them, you can instantiate a `TextMSA` object yourself, e.g.:
#     
# ```python
# seq1 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name="seq1", sequence="WVPKQDFT")
# seq2 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name="seq2", sequence="WL--PQGE")
# msa  = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(name="msa", sequences=[seq1, seq2])
# ```
#
# Because we need a `DigitalMSA` to build the HMM, you will have to convert it first:
#     
# ```python
# msa_d = msa.digitize(alphabet) 
# ```
# </div>

# ## Building an HMM
#
# Now that we have a multiple alignment loaded in memory, we can build a pHMM using a `pyhmmer.plan7.Builder`. This also requires a Plan7 background model to compute the transition probabilities.

builder = pyhmmer.plan7.Builder(alphabet)
background = pyhmmer.plan7.Background(alphabet)
hmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(msa, background)

# <div class="alert alert-warning">
#
# Warning
#     
# HMMs must always have a name. The `Builder` will attempt to use the `MSA` name, but in the event your alignment file does not contain a name for the whole alignment (for instance, a `#=GF ID` line in a [Stockholm file](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_format)), this method will fail:
#     
# ```python
# >>> anonymous_msa = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(sequences=[seq1, seq2])
# >>> builder.build_msa(anonymous_msa)
# Traceback (most recent call last):
#   File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
# ValueError: Could not build HMM: Unable to name the HMM.
# ```    
#
# If your alignment is missing a name, you can assign one manually by setting the `MSA.name` property, e.g.:
#
# ```python
# msa.name = "protein_family_01"
# ```
#     
# </div>

# We can have a look at the consensus sequence of the HMM with the `consensus` property:

hmm.consensus

# ## Saving the resulting HMM

# Now that we have an HMM, we can save it to a file to avoid having to rebuild it every time. Using the `HMM.write` method lets us write the HMM in ASCII or binary format to an arbitrary file. The resulting file will also be compatible with the `hmmsearch` binary if you wish to use that one instead of PyHMMER.

with open("LuxC.hmm", "wb") as output_file:
    hmm.write(output_file)

# ## Applying the HMM to a sequence database

# Once a pHMM has been obtained, it can be applied to a sequence database with the `pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline` object. Let's iterate over the protein sequences in a FASTA to see if our new HMM gets any hits:

pipeline = pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline(alphabet, background=background)
with pyhmmer.easel.SequenceFile("data/seqs/LuxC.faa", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as seq_file:
    hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, seq_file)

# We can then query the `TopHits` object to access the domain hits in the sequences:

ali = hits[0].domains[0].alignment
print(ali)

# Finally, we can save the results in tabular format similar to what `hmmsearch` would have produced:

with open("LuxC.domtbl", "wb") as f:
    hits.write(f, format="domains")

Build the LuxC profile and report protein domain hits

The published solver question is below. Reference answers and grading code are separate from solver inputs.

Solver question

autonomous-runs/124/explorer-evidence/native/tasks/autonomous-panel-124/instruction.md

Build a profile HMM for the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family and search a protein sequence database

Objective

Build a profile HMM from a multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase protein family, then use that HMM to search a protein sequence database. Deliver the built profile HMM and the search results in standard HMMER3 output formats.

Inputs (under inputs/)

  • inputs/msa/LuxC.sto — Stockholm-format multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family (13 protein sequences, 400 alignment columns). The alignment header carries family annotation: the alignment name, accession, description, and the GA (gathering), TC (trusted) and NC (noise) cutoff score lines.
  • inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa — FASTA file of protein sequences; the sequence database to search.

Method

  1. Read the Stockholm alignment as a single amino-acid multiple sequence alignment (all 13 sequences).
  2. Build the profile HMM from the alignment using standard HMMER3 profile construction with default hmmbuild settings: relative sequence weighting by the Henikoff position-based scheme, effective sequence number by relative-entropy targeting, amino-acid mixture Dirichlet priors, default position-architecting thresholds, and E-value calibration of the MSV/Viterbi/Forward score statistics against the standard amino-acid background distribution. The model must be named after the alignment name recorded in the file, must carry the alignment accession, and must carry the alignment's GA/TC/NC cutoff annotations through unchanged.
  3. Search the protein database with this HMM using standard hmmsearch default settings: local alignment mode, per-sequence (hit) reporting threshold E ≤ 10, per-domain reporting threshold E ≤ 10, the default MSV/Viterbi/Forward pipeline filtering, and E-values computed from the actual number of sequences searched.
  4. Use the same standard amino-acid background frequencies for both building and searching.

Any software implementing HMMER3 profile construction and search may be used (e.g., the HMMER3 binaries, pyhmmer, or a compatible work-alike). No network access is available. Resources: CPU-only, at most 8 GB RAM; the computation is small and completes in minutes at most (the reference run takes well under one second on this data).

Required outputs (under outputs/)

1. outputs/LuxC.hmm — the profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII text format: a header containing the model name derived from the alignment name, the alignment accession, the model length (400 match positions), sequence count and effective sequence number, the HMM checksum, the GA/TC/NC cutoff scores carried from the alignment, and the local-mode calibration statistics lines (MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD parameters), followed by the per-position emission, insert and transition parameters for all 400 model positions, terminated with //. The DATE build-timestamp line and the COM command-line line are run-specific and may differ between runs; all other content is fixed scientific content.

2. outputs/LuxC.domtbl — the search results in HMMER hmmsearch domain-table format (--domtblout style): leading comment lines beginning with #, then exactly one row per reported domain with the standard column order: target name, target accession, target length, query (HMM) name, query accession, query length, full-sequence E-value, full-sequence score, full-sequence bias, domain number (and total), conditional and independent per-domain E-values, per-domain score and bias, HMM coordinates (from/to), alignment coordinates (from/to), envelope coordinates (from/to), average posterior accuracy, and target description. Rows must follow the hmmsearch domain-table ordering convention (best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules). Only domains passing the stated reporting thresholds appear; the set of reported target sequences, the number of domains per sequence, and their coordinates are part of the requested scientific content — do not pad or prune rows heuristically, let the thresholds decide.

Cross-file consistency: the query name, accession and length reported in the domain table must match the model written to outputs/LuxC.hmm.

Acceptance rules

Acceptance rules (addendum to the task question)

Compared artifacts

Exactly two files are graded, read from the solver's output root at the declared paths: LuxC.hmm (HMMER3 plan7 ASCII profile HMM) and LuxC.domtbl (hmmsearch domain table). Each file must be present at its declared path; a file placed under an extra outputs/ subdirectory inside the output root is at the wrong path and is treated as missing. Values are compared against the reference outputs.

LuxC.hmm (HMMER3 ASCII profile)

  • Ignored (run-specific): the HMMER3/f version banner line, the DATE build-timestamp line and the COM command-line line. These lines are excluded from every comparison; the grader does not compare the HMMER version string.
  • Compared exactly: the model name (NAME, from the alignment #=GF ID), accession (ACC), description (DESC), model length (LENG, 400 match positions), sequence count (NSEQ), HMM checksum (CKSUM, integer), and the GA/TC/NC cutoff score pairs (values parsed as real numbers; these are the alignment's cutoff lines carried through unchanged). The presence of ALPH, RF, MM, CONS, CS, MAP, EFFN, NSEQ and the three STATS LOCAL calibration lines is required, as is the trailing // terminator.
  • Compared numerically: EFFN (effective sequence number), the STATS LOCAL MSV, STATS LOCAL VITERBI and STATS LOCAL FORWARD parameters, the COMPO background line, and every per-position match emission, insert emission and transition row for all 400 model positions in position order. Each of these values is compared with an absolute tolerance of 2×10⁻⁵ (all reference values are indistinguishable beyond their 5-decimal print width); * (zero probability) and the m->m-style header tokens and consensus/MAP characters are compared as exact text. Trailing whitespace and column alignment is not compared.
  • Structural requirement: the file must parse as an amino-acid plan7 HMM with a HMMER3 plan7 ASCII reader, declare a model length equal to the number of per-position parameter blocks, and terminate with //.

LuxC.domtbl (hmmsearch domain table)

  • Comment lines beginning with # are ignored as header text; their presence or exact wording is not compared.
  • Every data row is parsed into the standard 22 fixed columns plus the free-text description; a row with fewer than 22 fields fails. Rows are compared in file order, which is the hmmsearch ordering: best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules (in this reference there are no E-value ties, so the ranking is unambiguous).
  • Row count: the number of reported domain rows is compared exactly — the set of reported targets, the number of domains per target (columns "dom" and "of") and the total row count are requested scientific content. Padding with extra rows or pruning rows is a wrong answer.
  • Exact integer fields: target length (tlen), query length (qlen), domain index/total (#, of), and all HMM, alignment and envelope coordinates (hmm from/to, ali from/to, env from/to).
  • Numeric tolerance — scores and bias: full-sequence and per-domain scores and bias are printed with one decimal; a submission value passes if its absolute difference from the reference value is ≤ 0.06 (half a printed decimal unit plus floating-point rounding slack). This bounds a representation/rounding difference only; it is not a guarantee that every wrong scoring method is detected.
  • Numeric tolerance — E-values: full-sequence, conditional and independent per-domain E-values span many orders of magnitude and are compared with a relative rule: a submitted E-value passes if |submitted − reference| ≤ 0.05 × max(|submitted|, |reference|), i.e. within 5% of the larger of the two magnitudes. This is the reference/denominator convention that fixes the acceptance boundary.
  • Numeric tolerance — average posterior accuracy (acc): absolute difference ≤ 0.006 (half a printed 2-decimal unit plus rounding slack).
  • Exact text fields: target name, target accession (- when absent), query name, query accession, and the target description column.
  • Rejected values: any non-finite or unparsable numeric value (including nan, inf, -inf, *) fails the corresponding check; a negative or out-of-range domain index, or missing fields, also fails.

Cross-file consistency

The query name, accession and length in every LuxC.domtbl row must equal the NAME, ACC and LENG of the profile written to LuxC.hmm.

General

Missing files, unreadable or malformed content, and files failing to parse with a HMMER3-format reader are failed checks, not successful runs. The grader compares parsed scientific content only; it does not compare timestamps, command lines, file byte hashes, HMMER version strings, comment headers in the domain table, or trailing-whitespace/indentation differences.

Task directories

Read the supplied inputs from /workspace/inputs/. Write all required output files under /workspace/outputs/, using the relative filenames specified above. The working directory is /workspace. Aliases /inputs/ and /outputs/ refer to these same directories.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Acceptance grader for the LuxC profile-HMM build and database search task.

Compares the two declared outputs (LuxC.hmm, LuxC.domtbl) against the
reference outputs, using HMMER3 plan7 ASCII and hmmsearch domain-table
parsing conventions.
"""

import argparse
import json
import math
import os
import sys

HMM_REL = "LuxC.hmm"
DOMTBL_REL = "LuxC.domtbl"

# Tolerances (documented in the public acceptance rules)
TOL_HMM = 2e-5          # HMMER3 ASCII prints parameters with 5 decimals
TOL_SCORE = 0.06         # hmmsearch domtbl prints scores/bias with 1 decimal
TOL_ACC = 0.006         # domtbl prints average posterior accuracy with 2 decimals
TOL_INT_FIELD = 0.5     # integer-length/coordinate fields: effectively exact
TOL_EVALUE_REL = 0.05   # E-value relative tolerance (<= 5% of the larger magnitude)

IDENTITY_KEYS = ["NAME", "ACC", "DESC", "LENG", "NSEQ", "CKSUM", "GA", "TC", "NC"]


def try_float(token):
    """Parse a printable numeric token; reject '*' and non-finite values."""
    try:
        value = float(token)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return None
    if math.isnan(value) or math.isinf(value):
        return None
    return value


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- HMM parsing

def load_hmm_tokens(path):
    """Tokenize an HMMER3 ASCII HMM, skipping run-specific lines.

    The HMMER3/f version banner, DATE and COM lines are run-specific and
    excluded from every comparison. Everything else is tokenized on
    whitespace so formatting/indentation differences do not matter.
    """
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        text = fh.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    rows = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if not line:
            continue
        tokens = line.split()
        head = tokens[0]
        if head.startswith("HMMER3/") or head in ("DATE", "COM"):
            continue
        rows.append(tokens)
    return rows


def split_hmm_rows(rows):
    """Split parsed rows into annotation rows (by header key) and data rows."""
    annotation = []
    data = []
    for tokens in rows:
        if tokens[0] in IDENTITY_KEYS:
            annotation.append(tokens)
        else:
            data.append(tokens)
    return annotation, data


def count_model_positions(rows):
    """Return the number of match-state positions implied by the row layout.

    HMMER3 plan7 ASCII layout after the per-position column header:
      - a "m->m m->i m->d i->m i->i d->m d->d" transition-labels row,
      - a "COMPO" block of 3 rows (compound emission, insert, transition),
      - then one 3-row block per model position (match emissions, insert
        emissions, transitions), terminated by the // line.
    """
    try:
        hmm_idx = next(i for i, t in enumerate(rows) if t[0] == "HMM")
    except StopIteration:
        return None
    if hmm_idx + 5 >= len(rows):
        return None
    if rows[hmm_idx + 1][0] != "m->m":
        return None
    if rows[hmm_idx + 2][0] != "COMPO":
        return None
    rest = rows[hmm_idx + 5:]
    if not rest:
        return None
    while rest and rest[-1][0] == "//":
        rest = rest[:-1]
    if not rest or len(rest) % 3 != 0:
        return None
    return len(rest) // 3


def annotation_value(rows, key):
    for tokens in rows:
        if tokens[0] == key:
            return tokens[1] if len(tokens) > 1 else ""
    return None


# ------------------------------------------------------------- domtbl parsing

# 0-based column indices, hmmsearch --domtblout domain table layout (22 fixed
# fields + free-text description).
DOMTBL_EVALUE_COLS = (6, 11, 12)
DOMTBL_SCORE_COLS = (7, 13)
DOMTBL_BIAS_COLS = (8, 14)
DOMTBL_ACC_COL = 21
DOMTBL_INT_COLS = (2, 5, 9, 10, 15, 16, 17, 18, 19, 20)
DOMTBL_STR_COLS = (0, 1, 3, 4, 22)


def load_domtbl_rows(path):
    """Parse the domain table into field lists in file order.

    Comment lines (leading '#') are header text and not compared. Each data
    row must split into the 22 standard fields; an optional 23rd field is the
    free-text description.
    """
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        text = fh.read().decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    rows = []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip("\r")
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        if line.lstrip().startswith("#"):
            continue
        fields = line.split(None, 22)
        if len(fields) < 22:
            raise ValueError("domain-table row has fewer than 22 fields")
        if len(fields) == 22:
            fields = fields + [""]
        rows.append(fields)
    return rows


def domtbl_row_is_structurally_valid(fields):
    """Check that every numeric column parses as a finite number."""
    for idx in DOMTBL_INT_COLS:
        if try_float(fields[idx]) is None:
            return False, "column %d (%s) is not a finite number" % (idx + 1, fields[idx])
    for idx in DOMTBL_EVALUE_COLS:
        if try_float(fields[idx]) is None:
            return False, "E-value column %d (%s) is not a finite number" % (idx + 1, fields[idx])
    for idx in DOMTBL_SCORE_COLS + DOMTBL_BIAS_COLS:
        if try_float(fields[idx]) is None:
            return False, "score/bias column %d (%s) is not a finite number" % (idx + 1, fields[idx])
    if try_float(fields[DOMTBL_ACC_COL]) is None:
        return False, "accuracy column is not a finite number"
    dom_num = try_float(fields[9])
    dom_total = try_float(fields[10])
    if dom_num is None or dom_total is None or dom_num < 1 or dom_num > dom_total:
        return False, "domain index out of range"
    return True, ""


# ----------------------------------------------------------- comparison logic

def compare_hmm_token_rows(sub_rows, ref_rows, tol, label):
    """Compare equal-length tokenized HMM rows numerically or textually."""
    if len(sub_rows) != len(ref_rows):
        return False, "%s: line count %d does not match reference %d" % (label, len(sub_rows), len(ref_rows))
    for lineno, (stokens, rtokens) in enumerate(zip(sub_rows, ref_rows), start=1):
        if len(stokens) != len(rtokens):
            return False, "%s line %d: field count %d != %d" % (label, lineno, len(stokens), len(rtokens))
        for pos, (s, r) in enumerate(zip(stokens, rtokens)):
            fs, fr = try_float(s), try_float(r)
            if fs is not None and fr is not None:
                if abs(fs - fr) > tol:
                    return False, "%s line %d field %d: %s != %s" % (label, lineno, pos + 1, s, r)
            elif s != r:
                return False, "%s line %d field %d: %r != %r" % (label, lineno, pos + 1, s, r)
    return True, ""


def annotation_map(annotation_rows):
    """Map header key -> value tokens (each HMMER3 header key appears once)."""
    amap = {}
    for tokens in annotation_rows:
        key = tokens[0]
        if key in amap:
            raise ValueError("duplicate header key %s" % key)
        amap[key] = tokens[1:]
    return amap


def compare_hmm_annotation(sub_rows, ref_rows, tol):
    """Compare annotation lines key-by-key, order-insensitively."""
    try:
        sub_map = annotation_map(sub_rows)
        ref_map = annotation_map(ref_rows)
    except ValueError as exc:
        return False, "model header: %s" % exc
    if set(sub_map) != set(ref_map):
        missing = sorted(set(ref_map) - set(sub_map))
        extra = sorted(set(sub_map) - set(ref_map))
        return False, ("model header key set differs; missing %s, unexpected %s"
                       % (",".join(missing) or "-", ",".join(extra) or "-"))
    for key in sorted(ref_map):
        stokens, rtokens = sub_map[key], ref_map[key]
        if len(stokens) != len(rtokens):
            return False, "model header %s: %d values, expected %d" % (key, len(stokens), len(rtokens))
        for pos, (s, r) in enumerate(zip(stokens, rtokens)):
            fs, fr = try_float(s), try_float(r)
            if fs is not None and fr is not None:
                if abs(fs - fr) > tol:
                    return False, "model header %s value %d: %s != %s" % (key, pos + 1, s, r)
            elif s != r:
                return False, "model header %s value %d: %r != %r" % (key, pos + 1, s, r)
    return True, ""


def compare_domtbl_row(sub, ref, idx):
    for col in DOMTBL_STR_COLS:
        if col >= len(sub) or col >= len(ref):
            return False, "row %d column %d missing" % (idx + 1, col + 1)
        if sub[col] != ref[col]:
            return False, "row %d column %d: %r != %r" % (idx + 1, col + 1, sub[col], ref[col])
    for col in DOMTBL_INT_COLS:
        fs, fr = try_float(sub[col]), try_float(ref[col])
        if fs is None or fr is None or abs(fs - fr) > TOL_INT_FIELD:
            return False, "row %d column %d (coordinate/length): %s != %s" % (idx + 1, col + 1, sub[col], ref[col])
    for col in DOMTBL_EVALUE_COLS:
        fs, fr = try_float(sub[col]), try_float(ref[col])
        if fs is None or fr is None:
            return False, "row %d column %d: non-finite E-value" % (idx + 1, col + 1)
        if abs(fs - fr) > TOL_EVALUE_REL * max(abs(fs), abs(fr)):
            return False, "row %d column %d (E-value): %s != %s" % (idx + 1, col + 1, sub[col], ref[col])
    for col in DOMTBL_SCORE_COLS + DOMTBL_BIAS_COLS:
        fs, fr = try_float(sub[col]), try_float(ref[col])
        # scores/bias are printed with 1 decimal; half a printed unit plus
        # floating-point rounding slack is the acceptance boundary
        if fs is None or fr is None or abs(fs - fr) > TOL_SCORE:
            return False, "row %d column %d (score/bias): %s != %s" % (idx + 1, col + 1, sub[col], ref[col])
    fs, fr = try_float(sub[DOMTBL_ACC_COL]), try_float(ref[DOMTBL_ACC_COL])
    if fs is None or fr is None or abs(fs - fr) > TOL_ACC:
        return False, "row %d accuracy column: %s != %s" % (idx + 1, sub[DOMTBL_ACC_COL], ref[DOMTBL_ACC_COL])
    return True, ""


# ------------------------------------------------------------------- grading

class Registry(object):
    def __init__(self):
        self.checks = []

    def record(self, check_id, passed, message):
        self.checks.append({"id": check_id, "passed": bool(passed), "message": message})


def grade(reference_dir, submission_dir):
    registry = Registry()

    ref_hmm_path = os.path.join(reference_dir, HMM_REL)
    sub_hmm_path = os.path.join(submission_dir, HMM_REL)
    ref_dom_path = os.path.join(reference_dir, DOMTBL_REL)
    sub_dom_path = os.path.join(submission_dir, DOMTBL_REL)

    # ---- reference side (guaranteed present) ------------------------------
    ref_hmm_tokens = load_hmm_tokens(ref_hmm_path)
    ref_annotation, ref_data = split_hmm_rows(ref_hmm_tokens)
    ref_n_positions = count_model_positions(ref_hmm_tokens)
    ref_dom_rows = load_domtbl_rows(ref_dom_path)

    # ---- check: hmm_ascii_structure ---------------------------------------
    check_id = "hmm_ascii_structure"
    ok = True
    msgs = []
    if not os.path.isfile(sub_hmm_path):
        registry.record(check_id, False, "required output %s is missing" % HMM_REL)
    else:
        try:
            sub_hmm_tokens = load_hmm_tokens(sub_hmm_path)
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
            registry.record(check_id, False, "could not read %s: %s" % (HMM_REL, exc))
            sub_hmm_tokens = None
        if sub_hmm_tokens is not None:
            if not sub_hmm_tokens:
                ok = False
                msgs.append("%s contains no parseable content" % HMM_REL)
            else:
                if sub_hmm_tokens[-1][0] != "//":
                    ok = False
                    msgs.append("file is not terminated by a // line")
                n_pos = count_model_positions(sub_hmm_tokens)
                if n_pos is None:
                    ok = False
                    msgs.append("HMM column header / COMPO block layout is malformed")
                elif n_pos != ref_n_positions:
                    ok = False
                    msgs.append("model has %d match positions, expected the reference %d" % (n_pos, ref_n_positions))
                present = set(t[0] for t in sub_hmm_tokens if t)
                missing = [k for k in IDENTITY_KEYS + ["ALPH", "RF", "MM", "CONS", "CS", "MAP", "EFFN", "STATS", "HMM", "COMPO"] if k not in present]
                if missing:
                    ok = False
                    msgs.append("missing required header keys: %s" % ", ".join(missing))
            # native-reader validation (HMMER3 plan7 ASCII reader)
            parse_ok, parse_msg = True, ""
            try:
                import pyhmmer
                with pyhmmer.plan7.HMMFile(sub_hmm_path) as hf:
                    hmm_obj = hf.read()
                if hmm_obj.M != ref_n_positions:
                    parse_ok, parse_msg = False, "native reader reports %d model positions" % hmm_obj.M
                if hmm_obj.alphabet != pyhmmer.easel.Alphabet.amino():
                    parse_ok, parse_msg = False, "native reader reports a non-amino-acid alphabet"
            except Exception as exc:
                parse_ok = False
                parse_msg = "not readable as a valid HMMER3 ASCII profile HMM (%s)" % exc
            if not parse_ok:
                ok = False
                msgs.append(parse_msg)
        registry.record(check_id, ok, "; ".join(msgs) if msgs else
                        "LuxC.hmm is a structurally valid HMMER3 ASCII amino-acid profile HMM with %d match positions" % ref_n_positions)

    # ---- check: hmm_model_annotation ---------------------------------------
    check_id = "hmm_model_annotation"
    if not os.path.isfile(sub_hmm_path):
        registry.record(check_id, False, "required output %s is missing" % HMM_REL)
    else:
        try:
            sub_hmm_tokens = load_hmm_tokens(sub_hmm_path)
            sub_annotation, _sub_data = split_hmm_rows(sub_hmm_tokens)
            ok, msg = compare_hmm_annotation(sub_annotation, ref_annotation, TOL_HMM)
            registry.record(check_id, ok, msg if msg else
                            "NAME/ACC/DESC/LENG/NSEQ/CKSUM and GA/TC/NC cutoff lines match the reference model")
        except Exception as exc:
            registry.record(check_id, False, "could not compare model header: %s" % exc)

    # ---- check: hmm_model_parameters ---------------------------------------
    check_id = "hmm_model_parameters"
    if not os.path.isfile(sub_hmm_path):
        registry.record(check_id, False, "required output %s is missing" % HMM_REL)
    else:
        try:
            sub_hmm_tokens = load_hmm_tokens(sub_hmm_path)
            _sub_annotation, sub_data = split_hmm_rows(sub_hmm_tokens)
            # The model parameters: EFFN / calibration STATS lines, HMM column
            # header, COMPO block and every per-position block (emissions,
            # insert emissions, transitions and consensus/map characters).
            ok, msg = compare_hmm_token_rows(sub_data, ref_data, TOL_HMM, "model body")
            if ok:
                registry.record(check_id, True, "effective sequence number, MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD calibration "
                                "statistics, COMPO block and all %d per-position emission/insert/transition "
                                "parameters match the reference model" % ref_n_positions)
            else:
                registry.record(check_id, False, msg)
        except Exception as exc:
            registry.record(check_id, False, "could not compare model parameters: %s" % exc)

    # ---- check: domtbl_structure -------------------------------------------
    check_id = "domtbl_structure"
    if not os.path.isfile(sub_dom_path):
        registry.record(check_id, False, "required output %s is missing" % DOMTBL_REL)
    else:
        ok = True
        msgs = []
        sub_dom_rows = None
        try:
            sub_dom_rows = load_domtbl_rows(sub_dom_path)
        except Exception as exc:
            ok = False
            msgs.append("domain table is malformed: %s" % exc)
        if sub_dom_rows is not None:
            if not sub_dom_rows:
                ok = False
                msgs.append("domain table contains no data rows")
            for i, fields in enumerate(sub_dom_rows):
                valid, why = domtbl_row_is_structurally_valid(fields)
                if not valid:
                    ok = False
                    msgs.append("row %d: %s" % (i + 1, why))
                    break
        registry.record(check_id, ok, "; ".join(msgs) if msgs else
                        "LuxC.domtbl is a well-formed hmmsearch domain table with %d data rows" % len(sub_dom_rows or []))

    # ---- check: domtbl_hits -------------------------------------------------
    check_id = "domtbl_hits"
    if not os.path.isfile(sub_dom_path):
        registry.record(check_id, False, "required output %s is missing" % DOMTBL_REL)
    else:
        ok, msg = True, ""
        try:
            sub_dom_rows = load_domtbl_rows(sub_dom_path)
        except Exception as exc:
            sub_dom_rows = None
            ok, msg = False, "domain table is malformed: %s" % exc
        if sub_dom_rows is not None:
            if len(sub_dom_rows) != len(ref_dom_rows):
                ok, msg = False, ("domain table has %d rows, expected %d (reported targets and domains per "
                                  "target are requested scientific content; do not pad or prune)" % (len(sub_dom_rows), len(ref_dom_rows)))
            else:
                reasons = []
                for i, (sub_row, ref_row) in enumerate(zip(sub_dom_rows, ref_dom_rows)):
                    row_ok, why = compare_domtbl_row(sub_row, ref_row, i)
                    if not row_ok:
                        reasons.append(why)
                if reasons:
                    ok, msg = False, "row-by-row comparison failed (order-sensitive, best full-sequence E-value first): " + "; ".join(reasons[:5])
                else:
                    ok, msg = True, ("all %d reported domains match the reference in order: target identity, scores, "
                                    "E-values, coordinates and descriptions" % len(ref_dom_rows))
        registry.record(check_id, ok, msg if msg else "domain table matches")

    # ---- check: hmm_domtbl_query_consistency --------------------------------
    check_id = "hmm_domtbl_query_consistency"
    both = os.path.isfile(sub_hmm_path) and os.path.isfile(sub_dom_path)
    if not both:
        registry.record(check_id, False, "one or both of %s / %s is missing" % (HMM_REL, DOMTBL_REL))
    else:
        ok = True
        msgs = []
        try:
            sub_hmm_tokens = load_hmm_tokens(sub_hmm_path)
            sub_dom_rows = load_domtbl_rows(sub_dom_path)
            sub_name = annotation_value(sub_hmm_tokens, "NAME")
            sub_acc = annotation_value(sub_hmm_tokens, "ACC")
            sub_leng = try_float(annotation_value(sub_hmm_tokens, "LENG"))
            # the domtbl query columns must describe the model in LuxC.hmm,
            # which by the other checks must equal the reference model.
            for i, fields in enumerate(sub_dom_rows):
                qname = fields[3]
                qacc = fields[4]
                qlen = try_float(fields[5])
                if qname != sub_name or qacc != sub_acc or qlen is None or sub_leng is None or abs(qlen - sub_leng) > TOL_INT_FIELD:
                    ok = False
                    msgs.append("row %d: query %s/%s/%s does not match the model %s/%s/%s" %
                                (i + 1, qname, qacc, fields[5], sub_name, sub_acc, annotation_value(sub_hmm_tokens, "LENG")))
                    break
        except Exception as exc:
            ok = False
            msgs.append("could not verify cross-file consistency: %s" % exc)
        registry.record(check_id, ok, "; ".join(msgs) if msgs else
                        "every domain-table row reports the query name/accession/length of the profile HMM in %s" % HMM_REL)

    return {"passed": all(c["passed"] for c in registry.checks), "checks": registry.checks}


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Grade the LuxC profile HMM task outputs")
    parser.add_argument("--reference-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--submission-dir", required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--report", required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    report = grade(args.reference_dir, args.submission_dir)
    with open(args.report, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        json.dump(report, fh, indent=2)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import argparse
import os


def locate(root, rel):
    """Locate a required input file relative to the given input root."""
    for cand in (os.path.join(root, rel), os.path.join(root, "inputs", rel)):
        if os.path.exists(cand):
            return cand
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"required input {rel!r} not found under {root}")


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Build the LuxC profile HMM and search the protein database")
    parser.add_argument("--input-dir", required=True, help="Directory containing the supplied inputs")
    parser.add_argument("--output-dir", required=True, help="Directory to write the required outputs")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    import pyhmmer
    from pyhmmer import easel, plan7

    # Amino-acid alphabet used for reading, building, and searching.
    alphabet = easel.Alphabet.amino()

    # 1. Read the Stockholm alignment as one digital amino-acid MSA.
    msa_path = locate(args.input_dir, "msa/LuxC.sto")
    with easel.MSAFile(msa_path, digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as msa_file:
        msa = msa_file.read()

    # 2. Build the profile HMM with default HMMER3 construction settings.
    builder = plan7.Builder(alphabet)
    background = plan7.Background(alphabet)
    hmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(msa, background)

    # Write the profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII format.
    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)
    hmm_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, "LuxC.hmm")
    with open(hmm_path, "wb") as output_file:
        hmm.write(output_file)

    # 3. Search the protein sequence database with the built HMM,
    #    using hmmsearch defaults (local mode, E<=10 / domE<=10 thresholds,
    #    default MSV/Viterbi/Forward filtering, Z from the sequence count).
    pipeline = plan7.Pipeline(alphabet, background=background)
    seq_path = locate(args.input_dir, "seqs/LuxC.faa")
    with easel.SequenceFile(seq_path, digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as seq_file:
        hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, seq_file)

    # Write the search hits in hmmsearch domain-table format.
    domtbl_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, "LuxC.domtbl")
    with open(domtbl_path, "wb") as f:
        hits.write(f, format="domains")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Task Description:

Build a profile HMM for the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family and search a protein sequence database

Objective

Build a profile HMM from a multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase protein family, then use that HMM to search a protein sequence database. Deliver the built profile HMM and the search results in standard HMMER3 output formats.

Inputs (under inputs/)

  • inputs/msa/LuxC.sto — Stockholm-format multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family (13 protein sequences, 400 alignment columns). The alignment header carries family annotation: the alignment name, accession, description, and the GA (gathering), TC (trusted) and NC (noise) cutoff score lines.
  • inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa — FASTA file of protein sequences; the sequence database to search.

Method

  1. Read the Stockholm alignment as a single amino-acid multiple sequence alignment (all 13 sequences).
  2. Build the profile HMM from the alignment using standard HMMER3 profile construction with default hmmbuild settings: relative sequence weighting by the Henikoff position-based scheme, effective sequence number by relative-entropy targeting, amino-acid mixture Dirichlet priors, default position-architecting thresholds, and E-value calibration of the MSV/Viterbi/Forward score statistics against the standard amino-acid background distribution. The model must be named after the alignment name recorded in the file, must carry the alignment accession, and must carry the alignment's GA/TC/NC cutoff annotations through unchanged.
  3. Search the protein database with this HMM using standard hmmsearch default settings: local alignment mode, per-sequence (hit) reporting threshold E ≤ 10, per-domain reporting threshold E ≤ 10, the default MSV/Viterbi/Forward pipeline filtering, and E-values computed from the actual number of sequences searched.
  4. Use the same standard amino-acid background frequencies for both building and searching.

Any software implementing HMMER3 profile construction and search may be used (e.g., the HMMER3 binaries, pyhmmer, or a compatible work-alike). No network access is available. Resources: CPU-only, at most 8 GB RAM; the computation is small and completes in minutes at most (the reference run takes well under one second on this data).

Required outputs (under outputs/)

1. outputs/LuxC.hmm — the profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII text format: a header containing the model name derived from the alignment name, the alignment accession, the model length (400 match positions), sequence count and effective sequence number, the HMM checksum, the GA/TC/NC cutoff scores carried from the alignment, and the local-mode calibration statistics lines (MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD parameters), followed by the per-position emission, insert and transition parameters for all 400 model positions, terminated with //. The DATE build-timestamp line and the COM command-line line are run-specific and may differ between runs; all other content is fixed scientific content.

2. outputs/LuxC.domtbl — the search results in HMMER hmmsearch domain-table format (--domtblout style): leading comment lines beginning with #, then exactly one row per reported domain with the standard column order: target name, target accession, target length, query (HMM) name, query accession, query length, full-sequence E-value, full-sequence score, full-sequence bias, domain number (and total), conditional and independent per-domain E-values, per-domain score and bias, HMM coordinates (from/to), alignment coordinates (from/to), envelope coordinates (from/to), average posterior accuracy, and target description. Rows must follow the hmmsearch domain-table ordering convention (best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules). Only domains passing the stated reporting thresholds appear; the set of reported target sequences, the number of domains per sequence, and their coordinates are part of the requested scientific content — do not pad or prune rows heuristically, let the thresholds decide.

Cross-file consistency: the query name, accession and length reported in the domain table must match the model written to outputs/LuxC.hmm.

Acceptance rules

Acceptance rules (addendum to the task question)

Compared artifacts

Exactly two files are graded, read from the solver's output root at the declared paths: LuxC.hmm (HMMER3 plan7 ASCII profile HMM) and LuxC.domtbl (hmmsearch domain table). Each file must be present at its declared path; a file placed under an extra outputs/ subdirectory inside the output root is at the wrong path and is treated as missing. Values are compared against the reference outputs.

LuxC.hmm (HMMER3 ASCII profile)

  • Ignored (run-specific): the HMMER3/f version banner line, the DATE build-timestamp line and the COM command-line line. These lines are excluded from every comparison; the grader does not compare the HMMER version string.
  • Compared exactly: the model name (NAME, from the alignment #=GF ID), accession (ACC), description (DESC), model length (LENG, 400 match positions), sequence count (NSEQ), HMM checksum (CKSUM, integer), and the GA/TC/NC cutoff score pairs (values parsed as real numbers; these are the alignment's cutoff lines carried through unchanged). The presence of ALPH, RF, MM, CONS, CS, MAP, EFFN, NSEQ and the three STATS LOCAL calibration lines is required, as is the trailing // terminator.
  • Compared numerically: EFFN (effective sequence number), the STATS LOCAL MSV, STATS LOCAL VITERBI and STATS LOCAL FORWARD parameters, the COMPO background line, and every per-position match emission, insert emission and transition row for all 400 model positions in position order. Each of these values is compared with an absolute tolerance of 2×10⁻⁵ (all reference values are indistinguishable beyond their 5-decimal print width); * (zero probability) and the m->m-style header tokens and consensus/MAP characters are compared as exact text. Trailing whitespace and column alignment is not compared.
  • Structural requirement: the file must parse as an amino-acid plan7 HMM with a HMMER3 plan7 ASCII reader, declare a model length equal to the number of per-position parameter blocks, and terminate with //.

LuxC.domtbl (hmmsearch domain table)

  • Comment lines beginning with # are ignored as header text; their presence or exact wording is not compared.
  • Every data row is parsed into the standard 22 fixed columns plus the free-text description; a row with fewer than 22 fields fails. Rows are compared in file order, which is the hmmsearch ordering: best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules (in this reference there are no E-value ties, so the ranking is unambiguous).
  • Row count: the number of reported domain rows is compared exactly — the set of reported targets, the number of domains per target (columns "dom" and "of") and the total row count are requested scientific content. Padding with extra rows or pruning rows is a wrong answer.
  • Exact integer fields: target length (tlen), query length (qlen), domain index/total (#, of), and all HMM, alignment and envelope coordinates (hmm from/to, ali from/to, env from/to).
  • Numeric tolerance — scores and bias: full-sequence and per-domain scores and bias are printed with one decimal; a submission value passes if its absolute difference from the reference value is ≤ 0.06 (half a printed decimal unit plus floating-point rounding slack). This bounds a representation/rounding difference only; it is not a guarantee that every wrong scoring method is detected.
  • Numeric tolerance — E-values: full-sequence, conditional and independent per-domain E-values span many orders of magnitude and are compared with a relative rule: a submitted E-value passes if |submitted − reference| ≤ 0.05 × max(|submitted|, |reference|), i.e. within 5% of the larger of the two magnitudes. This is the reference/denominator convention that fixes the acceptance boundary.
  • Numeric tolerance — average posterior accuracy (acc): absolute difference ≤ 0.006 (half a printed 2-decimal unit plus rounding slack).
  • Exact text fields: target name, target accession (- when absent), query name, query accession, and the target description column.
  • Rejected values: any non-finite or unparsable numeric value (including nan, inf, -inf, *) fails the corresponding check; a negative or out-of-range domain index, or missing fields, also fails.

Cross-file consistency

The query name, accession and length in every LuxC.domtbl row must equal the NAME, ACC and LENG of the profile written to LuxC.hmm.

General

Missing files, unreadable or malformed content, and files failing to parse with a HMMER3-format reader are failed checks, not successful runs. The grader compares parsed scientific content only; it does not compare timestamps, command lines, file byte hashes, HMMER version strings, comment headers in the domain table, or trailing-whitespace/indentation differences.

        a single or a small number of queries. Note that parallelization
        on ``targets`` does not work with `~pyhmmer.easel.SequenceFile`
        targets.

Yields:
    `~pyhmmer.plan7.TopHits`: An object reporting *top hits* for each
    query, in the same order the queries were passed in the input.

Raises:
    `~pyhmmer.errors.AlphabetMismatch`: When any of the query HMMs
        and the sequences do not share the same alphabet.
    `RuntimeError`: When attempting to use ``targets`` parallel
        strategy with targets from a `~pyhmmer.easel.SequenceFile`.

Note:
    Any additional arguments passed to the `hmmsearch` function will be
    passed transparently to the `~pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline` to be created.
    For instance, to run a ``hmmsearch`` using a bitscore cutoffs of
    5 instead of the default E-value cutoff, use::

        >>> hits = next(hmmsearch(thioesterase, proteins, T=5))
        >>> hits[0].score
        8.601...

    Since *version 0.11.0*, ``mypy`` should be able to detection which
    keywords can be passed to `hmmsearch` using a `TypedDict` annotation.

.. versionadded:: 0.1.0

.. versionadded:: 0.11.1
   ``parallel`` argument to select parallelization strategy.

.. versionchanged:: 0.4.9

.. versionchanged:: 0.7.0

        Returns:
            (`HMM`, `Profile`, `OptimizedProfile`): A tuple containing the

        Raises:
            `~pyhmmer.errors.AlphabetMismatch`: When either ``msa`` or
                ``background`` have the wrong alphabet for this builder.
            `ValueError`: When the HMM cannot be created successfully
                from the input; the error message contains more details.

        Caution:
            HMMER requires that every HMM has a name, so the `Builder` will
            attempt to use the name of the sequence to name the HMM. Passing

from pyhmmer.plan7 import Builder, Background, Pipeline
abc = pyhmmer.easel.AA()
with MSAFile('inputs/msa/LuxC.sto', digital=True, alphabet=abc) as f: msa=f.read()
with SequenceFile('inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa', digital=True, alphabet=abc) as f: seqs=list(f)

with open('/tmp/LuxC.hmm','wb') as out: hmm.write(out)
pipeline = Pipeline(abc)
hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, seqs)

with open('/tmp/LuxC.domtbl','w') as out: hits.write(out, format='domains')
print('hit names', [h.name for h in hits])
print('domain counts', [len(h.domains) for h in hits])

import pyhmmer
from pyhmmer.easel import MSAFile, SequenceFile, SequenceBlock
from pyhmmer.plan7 import Builder, Background
abc = pyhmmer.easel.AA()
with MSAFile('inputs/msa/LuxC.sto', digital=True, alphabet=abc) as f:
    msa = f.read()
with SequenceFile('inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa', digital=True, alphabet=abc) as f:
    sequences = list(f)
block = SequenceBlock(sequences, alphabet=abc)
hmm, profile, optimized = Builder(abc).build_msa(msa, Background(abc))
print('sequence block length:', len(block), 'alphabet:', block.alphabet)
hits = next(pyhmmer.hmmer.hmmsearch(hmm, block))
print('reported hits:', len(hits))
print('targets:', [hit.name.decode() for hit in hits])
print('domains:', [len(hit.domains) for hit in hits])
with open('/tmp/LuxC.domtbl', 'w') as out:
    hits.write(out, format='domains')

import re
from pathlib import Path
from pyhmmer.plan7 import HMMFile
hmm_path = Path('/workspace/outputs/LuxC.hmm')
dom_path = Path('/workspace/outputs/LuxC.domtbl')
assert hmm_path.is_file() and dom_path.is_file()
with HMMFile(str(hmm_path)) as f:
    hmm = f.read()
assert hmm.name == 'LuxC'
assert hmm.accession == 'PF05893.5'
assert hmm.M == 400
header = hmm_path.read_text()
assert re.search(r'^LENG  400$', header, re.M)
assert header.rstrip().endswith('//')
assert all(re.search(rf'^{tag} ', header, re.M) for tag in ['ALPH', 'RF', 'MM', 'CONS', 'CS', 'MAP', 'EFFN', 'NSEQ', 'CKSUM', 'GA', 'TC', 'NC'])
assert len(re.findall(r'^STATS LOCAL ', header, re.M)) == 3
rows = [line.split() for line in dom_path.read_text().splitlines() if line and not line.startswith('#')]
assert len(rows) == 12
assert all(len(fields) >= 22 for fields in rows)
assert all(fields[3] == 'LuxC' and fields[4] == 'PF05893.5' and fields[5] == '400' for fields in rows)
assert all(fields[12] == '1' and fields[13] == '1' for fields in rows)
print('FINAL VALIDATION PASSED')
print('HMM:', hmm.name, hmm.accession, 'M=' + str(hmm.M), 'nseq=' + str(hmm.nseq), 'eff_nseq=' + str(hmm.eff_nseq), 'checksum=' + str(hmm.checksum))
print('Domain rows:', len(rows))
print('Output files:')

assert hmm.nseq == 13
assert hmm.checksum == 395769323

text = hmm_path.read_text()
lines = text.splitlines()
header = {line.split()[0]: line.split(None, 1)[1] for line in lines[:20] if line and not line.startswith('#') and not line.startswith('HMM ')}
assert header['NAME'] == 'LuxC'
assert header['ACC'] == 'PF05893.5'
assert header['DESC'] == 'Acyl-CoA reductase (LuxC)'

assert header['TC'] == '-133.50 -133.50'

terminator = next(i for i, line in enumerate(lines) if line == '//')

]

assert full_evalues == sorted(full_evalues)

print('Domain table: 12 reported domains, all query-consistent')

    "\n",
    "Note\n",

    "msa  = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(name=\"msa\", sequences=[seq1, seq2])\n",

# # Build an HMM from a multiple sequence alignment

import pyhmmer
pyhmmer.__version__

alphabet = pyhmmer.easel.Alphabet.amino()

# ## Loading the alignment

# A new HMM can be built from a single sequence, or from a multiple sequence alignment. Let's load an alignment in digital mode so that we can build our HMM. We can use a `MSAFile` to read an alignment from a file in one of the supported formats (such as [Stockholm](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-stockholm), [Clustal](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-clustal), [aligned FASTA](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-fasta), *etc*; see the `MSAFile` documentation for the complete list):

with pyhmmer.easel.MSAFile("data/msa/LuxC.sto", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as msa_file:
    msa = msa_file.read()

# <div class="alert alert-info">
#
# Note
#     
# In this example, we load a multiple sequence alignment from a file, but if your program produces alignment and you wish to make an HMM out of them, you can instantiate a `TextMSA` object yourself, e.g.:
#     
# ```python
# seq1 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name="seq1", sequence="WVPKQDFT")
# seq2 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name="seq2", sequence="WL--PQGE")
# msa  = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(name="msa", sequences=[seq1, seq2])
# ```
#
# Because we need a `DigitalMSA` to build the HMM, you will have to convert it first:
#     
# ```python
# msa_d = msa.digitize(alphabet) 
# ```
# </div>

# ## Building an HMM
#
# Now that we have a multiple alignment loaded in memory, we can build a pHMM using a `pyhmmer.plan7.Builder`. This also requires a Plan7 background model to compute the transition probabilities.

builder = pyhmmer.plan7.Builder(alphabet)
background = pyhmmer.plan7.Background(alphabet)
hmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(msa, background)

# <div class="alert alert-warning">
#
# Warning
#     
# HMMs must always have a name. The `Builder` will attempt to use the `MSA` name, but in the event your alignment file does not contain a name for the whole alignment (for instance, a `#=GF ID` line in a [Stockholm file](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_format)), this method will fail:
#     
# ```python
# >>> anonymous_msa = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(sequences=[seq1, seq2])
# >>> builder.build_msa(anonymous_msa)
# Traceback (most recent call last):
#   File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
# ValueError: Could not build HMM: Unable to name the HMM.
# ```    
#
# If your alignment is missing a name, you can assign one manually by setting the `MSA.name` property, e.g.:
#
# ```python
# msa.name = "protein_family_01"
# ```
#     
# </div>

# We can have a look at the consensus sequence of the HMM with the `consensus` property:

hmm.consensus

# ## Saving the resulting HMM

# Now that we have an HMM, we can save it to a file to avoid having to rebuild it every time. Using the `HMM.write` method lets us write the HMM in ASCII or binary format to an arbitrary file. The resulting file will also be compatible with the `hmmsearch` binary if you wish to use that one instead of PyHMMER.

with open("LuxC.hmm", "wb") as output_file:
    hmm.write(output_file)

# ## Applying the HMM to a sequence database

# Once a pHMM has been obtained, it can be applied to a sequence database with the `pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline` object. Let's iterate over the protein sequences in a FASTA to see if our new HMM gets any hits:

pipeline = pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline(alphabet, background=background)
with pyhmmer.easel.SequenceFile("data/seqs/LuxC.faa", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as seq_file:
    hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, seq_file)

# We can then query the `TopHits` object to access the domain hits in the sequences:

ali = hits[0].domains[0].alignment
print(ali)

# Finally, we can save the results in tabular format similar to what `hmmsearch` would have produced:

with open("LuxC.domtbl", "wb") as f:
    hits.write(f, format="domains")

Prompt

Actual system prompt

autonomous-runs/124/explorer-evidence/preparation/prepare/system-prompt.md

You prepare endpoint exports for an existing scientific notebook. Return one complete ReferencePlan JSON object matching the supplied response schema. This stage selects terminal scientific results and adds code to save those existing results to disk after the original script finishes. Return only the export code, not an edited or recopied source script. The controller appends it to the untouched baseline. This stage does not manage or execute the environment. There is one creation call and at most one repair after programmatic validation rejects the response or a controlled execution finds an export-code exception. These share one repair, not one each. If the controller returns validation feedback, return a complete corrected ReferencePlan, including unchanged fields. Keep the original scientific source and the export-only boundary fixed. A valid first response needs no repair. Keep explanations brief and nonduplicated.

Inputs

The user message supplies:

  • baseline_script: the complete, unmodified Python script from deterministic notebook conversion, with the original Markdown narrative retained as comments.
  • source: notebook identity and provenance.
  • conversion: the conversion receipt and source/script identities.
  • limits: the intended execution environment and resource/time limits.
  • During a runtime repair only, runtime_validation: the previous complete plan and the recorded execution error. Use this feedback to correct serialization of the same selected results. Preserve artifacts and excluded_outputs exactly, including paths and source evidence. Do not fix the analysis or select different results. Observations in an error log can be partial; do not invent data layout or new scientific computation to fill gaps.

You do not receive saved notebook outputs, embedded images, scientific data contents or tool access. A path or URL is not evidence that a resource has been inspected. Runtime, dependency availability and output properties remain unverified. Do not infer that a source has never run from a documentation setting.

Select terminal scientific results

First identify the scientific conclusions or end products the source aims to produce. Use its narrative and how results are interpreted, not a list of its sections, functions or stored variables. Include the independent scientific outcomes of all analysis branches in one task. Preparatory and diagnostic steps supporting those outcomes are not additional branches that need an export.

For each candidate result, distinguish its role:

  • An endpoint reports a scientific finding or final representation that the source interprets in its own right.
  • An intermediate prepares data or supplies another analysis step.
  • A diagnostic checks data quality, model fit or parameter choices in support of the analysis. Its being displayed, discussed or retained does not by itself make it a scientific endpoint.

Select the endpoints. A value used downstream can still qualify when the source also interprets it as an independent result; a value with no downstream consumer can still be only a diagnostic. Do not equate endpoints with either literal execution-graph leaves or objects surviving to the end. If the source does not establish an independent endpoint role, explain the exclusion or uncertainty rather than adding an export just for completeness.

Then locate the selected results in existing named variables or fields in the ORIGINAL script. They must still hold the intended values at script completion. If a result has been overwritten, deleted or is out of scope, explain its exclusion; do not insert earlier captures or rerun computation to recover it. A result displayed in a plot can qualify if its values already exist outside the plotting function. Values computed only inside plotting functions cannot.

Select fields by their scientific role before choosing a file format. This rule applies recursively: a table inside a mixed analysis object can itself mix final results with inputs, preprocessing statistics and diagnostics. Export only the selected endpoint fields and the identifiers/context needed to interpret them; do not copy all columns or dump a whole object because it is convenient. A standalone result table or embedding may be exported whole when its contents meet this rule. Preserve its meaningful result fields and identifiers, explaining any omissions. Selecting stored fields is allowed; changing the analyzed population or adding scientific computation is not. Output size alone does not determine eligibility.

Explain meaningful exclusions and any independent outcome without an eligible stored result in excluded_outputs. Do not enumerate every processing step. If no eligible terminal result can be exported, return disposition=reject. Excluding an output never permits skipping its original computation.

Save existing values only

Serialization means writing existing values and their identifiers to files. Use native writers or straightforward file-format conversion. Preserve values, identifiers, labels and ordering of the selected final-state results. A later filtered or overwritten object does not preserve an earlier result merely because it has the same variable name.

Do not add scientific computation for exports: no new filtering, ranking, aggregation, normalization, scaling, statistical tests or reconstruction of values computed inside plotting functions. Do not capture a previously unnamed standalone expression by assigning it to a new variable. Values inside an already named source object are eligible; a result held only inside a plotting function is not. Do not change plotting calls or add figure capture. Explain excluded plot-only results instead of claiming their numerical content was exported.

File-writing code may introduce output paths and serialization helpers, but not new scientific results. Put any needed imports in the appended export code, using names that do not overwrite source results. Do not recompute an analysis or call it again to obtain an export. Do not change the original inputs, methods, parameters, randomness, filtering, annotations, error handling or execution order. Keep the original analysis and comments intact, including branches whose outputs are excluded. Preserve source-level reductions; add none. Do not suppress analysis errors.

Required response

  • disposition: prepare or reject.
  • explanation: a brief reason and account of the added export code.
  • export_code: only the Python code to append at the end of the baseline, including any imports needed for saving files. Do not include the baseline, patches, insertion instructions, Markdown fences or future imports. Write endpoint files under /work/outputs, creating that directory if needed. Use only eligible original results still accessible at completion. For disposition=reject, this field may be empty.
  • artifacts: one inventory of endpoint files. Each entry has a path relative to /work/outputs (for example result.csv for /work/outputs/result.csv), a brief description of the terminal result, and source_evidence explaining why this is an endpoint based on the source analysis goals, and identifying the existing variable or object field and where the original script produces it. Cite the source narrative or use that establishes its endpoint role; mere persistence or a function name is not evidence of that role. Prefer interoperable formats. Several existing endpoint values may share a file if their identities remain explicit. Keep this inventory consistent with the export code: every declared path must be written under that exact name, with no placeholder or undeclared output filenames. Check that correspondence before returning the response.
  • excluded_outputs: meaningful non-target outputs and branches with no eligible terminal result, with a brief reason. Do not enumerate every intermediate.
  • unresolved_assumptions: specific questions for subsequent inspection or execution; do not invent observed dimensions, values, timing or resource use.

The controller preserves the returned export code and constructs the reference script as the original baseline, two newlines, then the export code. It checks response structure and combined Python syntax without executing code, and computes the source diff, file sizes and hashes. Do not generate those records. These checks do not prove terminal-result selection, scientific fidelity or successful execution.

Boundary with execution

The execution stage owns dependency discovery and installation, the Python project and uv lockfile, system packages, input downloads, caches and offline path adaptation. It can use an LLM with tools to inspect and diagnose concrete failures. Ordinary script execution is programmatic. Preparation must not return an environment manifest or staging script, install packages, rewrite retrieval code, choose package versions or claim an environment works. Leave original input-loading code unchanged for execution-stage adaptation and review.

The later scientific run remains CPU-only and offline, with original inputs staged during network-enabled setup. The supplied limits apply; uncertainty about fit is an execution question, not permission to simplify the analysis. Original responses and validation failures are preserved. The controller may request one corrected response for a validation failure; this does not authorize repairing the scientific source or retrying transport failures. Source analysis defects must not be repaired by changing the science. Distinguish a known defect from an untested assumption and explain rejection precisely.

# ---
# jupyter:
#   jupytext:
#     text_representation:
#       extension: .py
#       format_name: nomarker
#       format_version: '1.0'
#       jupytext_version: 1.19.6
#   kernelspec:
#     display_name: Python 3 (ipykernel)
#     language: python
#     name: python3
# ---

# # Build an HMM from a multiple sequence alignment

import pyhmmer
pyhmmer.__version__

alphabet = pyhmmer.easel.Alphabet.amino()

# ## Loading the alignment

# A new HMM can be built from a single sequence, or from a multiple sequence alignment. Let's load an alignment in digital mode so that we can build our HMM. We can use a `MSAFile` to read an alignment from a file in one of the supported formats (such as [Stockholm](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-stockholm), [Clustal](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-clustal), [aligned FASTA](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-fasta), *etc*; see the `MSAFile` documentation for the complete list):

with pyhmmer.easel.MSAFile("data/msa/LuxC.sto", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as msa_file:
    msa = msa_file.read()

# <div class="alert alert-info">
#
# Note
#     
# In this example, we load a multiple sequence alignment from a file, but if your program produces alignment and you wish to make an HMM out of them, you can instantiate a `TextMSA` object yourself, e.g.:
#     
# ```python
# seq1 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name="seq1", sequence="WVPKQDFT")
# seq2 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name="seq2", sequence="WL--PQGE")
# msa  = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(name="msa", sequences=[seq1, seq2])
# ```
#
# Because we need a `DigitalMSA` to build the HMM, you will have to convert it first:
#     
# ```python
# msa_d = msa.digitize(alphabet) 
# ```
# </div>

# ## Building an HMM
#
# Now that we have a multiple alignment loaded in memory, we can build a pHMM using a `pyhmmer.plan7.Builder`. This also requires a Plan7 background model to compute the transition probabilities.

builder = pyhmmer.plan7.Builder(alphabet)
background = pyhmmer.plan7.Background(alphabet)
hmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(msa, background)

# <div class="alert alert-warning">
#
# Warning
#     
# HMMs must always have a name. The `Builder` will attempt to use the `MSA` name, but in the event your alignment file does not contain a name for the whole alignment (for instance, a `#=GF ID` line in a [Stockholm file](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_format)), this method will fail:
#     
# ```python
# >>> anonymous_msa = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(sequences=[seq1, seq2])
# >>> builder.build_msa(anonymous_msa)
# Traceback (most recent call last):
#   File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
# ValueError: Could not build HMM: Unable to name the HMM.
# ```    
#
# If your alignment is missing a name, you can assign one manually by setting the `MSA.name` property, e.g.:
#
# ```python
# msa.name = "protein_family_01"
# ```
#     
# </div>

# We can have a look at the consensus sequence of the HMM with the `consensus` property:

hmm.consensus

# ## Saving the resulting HMM

# Now that we have an HMM, we can save it to a file to avoid having to rebuild it every time. Using the `HMM.write` method lets us write the HMM in ASCII or binary format to an arbitrary file. The resulting file will also be compatible with the `hmmsearch` binary if you wish to use that one instead of PyHMMER.

with open("LuxC.hmm", "wb") as output_file:
    hmm.write(output_file)

# ## Applying the HMM to a sequence database

# Once a pHMM has been obtained, it can be applied to a sequence database with the `pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline` object. Let's iterate over the protein sequences in a FASTA to see if our new HMM gets any hits:

pipeline = pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline(alphabet, background=background)
with pyhmmer.easel.SequenceFile("data/seqs/LuxC.faa", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as seq_file:
    hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, seq_file)

# We can then query the `TopHits` object to access the domain hits in the sequences:

ali = hits[0].domains[0].alignment
print(ali)

# Finally, we can save the results in tabular format similar to what `hmmsearch` would have produced:

with open("LuxC.domtbl", "wb") as f:
    hits.write(f, format="domains")


import os

os.makedirs("/work/outputs", exist_ok=True)

with open("/work/outputs/LuxC.hmm", "wb") as _export_hmm_file:
    hmm.write(_export_hmm_file)

with open("/work/outputs/LuxC.domtbl", "wb") as _export_hits_file:
    hits.write(_export_hits_file, format="domains")
