    "instruction": "# Acceptance rules (addendum to the task question)\n\n## Compared artifacts\nExactly two files are graded, read from the solver's output root at the declared paths: `LuxC.hmm` (HMMER3 plan7 ASCII profile HMM) and `LuxC.domtbl` (hmmsearch domain table). Each file must be present at its declared path; a file placed under an extra `outputs/` subdirectory inside the output root is at the wrong path and is treated as missing. Values are compared against the reference outputs.\n\n## LuxC.hmm (HMMER3 ASCII profile)\n- **Ignored (run-specific):** the `HMMER3/f` version banner line, the `DATE` build-timestamp line and the `COM` command-line line. These lines are excluded from every comparison; the grader does not compare the HMMER version string.\n- **Compared exactly:** the model name (`NAME`, from the alignment `#=GF ID`), accession (`ACC`), description (`DESC`), model length (`LENG`, 400 match positions), sequence count (`NSEQ`), HMM checksum (`CKSUM`, integer), and the `GA`/`TC`/`NC` cutoff score pairs (values parsed as real numbers; these are the alignment's cutoff lines carried through unchanged). The presence of `ALPH`, `RF`, `MM`, `CONS`, `CS`, `MAP`, `EFFN`, `NSEQ` and the three `STATS LOCAL` calibration lines is required, as is the trailing `//` terminator.\n- **Compared numerically:** `EFFN` (effective sequence number), the `STATS LOCAL MSV`, `STATS LOCAL VITERBI` and `STATS LOCAL FORWARD` parameters, the `COMPO` background line, and every per-position match emission, insert emission and transition row for all 400 model positions in position order. Each of these values is compared with an absolute tolerance of 2\u00d710\u207b\u2075 (all reference values are indistinguishable beyond their 5-decimal print width); `*` (zero probability) and the `m->m`-style header tokens and consensus/MAP characters are compared as exact text. Trailing whitespace and column alignment is not compared.\n- **Structural requirement:** the file must parse as an amino-acid plan7 HMM with a HMMER3 plan7 ASCII reader, declare a model length equal to the number of per-position parameter blocks, and terminate with `//`.\n\n## LuxC.domtbl (hmmsearch domain table)\n- Comment lines beginning with `#` are ignored as header text; their presence or exact wording is not compared.\n- Every data row is parsed into the standard 22 fixed columns plus the free-text description; a row with fewer than 22 fields fails. Rows are compared **in file order**, which is the hmmsearch ordering: best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules (in this reference there are no E-value ties, so the ranking is unambiguous).\n- **Row count:** the number of reported domain rows is compared exactly \u2014 the set of reported targets, the number of domains per target (columns \"dom\" and \"of\") and the total row count are requested scientific content. Padding with extra rows or pruning rows is a wrong answer.\n- **Exact integer fields:** target length (`tlen`), query length (`qlen`), domain index/total (`#`, `of`), and all HMM, alignment and envelope coordinates (`hmm from/to`, `ali from/to`, `env from/to`).\n- **Numeric tolerance \u2014 scores and bias:** full-sequence and per-domain scores and bias are printed with one decimal; a submission value passes if its absolute difference from the reference value is \u2264 0.06 (half a printed decimal unit plus floating-point rounding slack). This bounds a representation/rounding difference only; it is not a guarantee that every wrong scoring method is detected.\n- **Numeric tolerance \u2014 E-values:** full-sequence, conditional and independent per-domain E-values span many orders of magnitude and are compared with a *relative* rule: a submitted E-value passes if |submitted \u2212 reference| \u2264 0.05 \u00d7 max(|submitted|, |reference|), i.e. within 5% of the larger of the two magnitudes. This is the reference/denominator convention that fixes the acceptance boundary.\n- **Numeric tolerance \u2014 average posterior accuracy (`acc`):** absolute difference \u2264 0.006 (half a printed 2-decimal unit plus rounding slack).\n- **Exact text fields:** target name, target accession (`-` when absent), query name, query accession, and the target description column.\n- **Rejected values:** any non-finite or unparsable numeric value (including `nan`, `inf`, `-inf`, `*`) fails the corresponding check; a negative or out-of-range domain index, or missing fields, also fails.\n\n## Cross-file consistency\nThe query name, accession and length in every `LuxC.domtbl` row must equal the `NAME`, `ACC` and `LENG` of the profile written to `LuxC.hmm`.\n\n## General\nMissing files, unreadable or malformed content, and files failing to parse with a HMMER3-format reader are failed checks, not successful runs. The grader compares parsed scientific content only; it does not compare timestamps, command lines, file byte hashes, HMMER version strings, comment headers in the domain table, or trailing-whitespace/indentation differences.",
    "rationale": "SELECTION. The task has exactly two declared endpoints \u2014 LuxC.hmm (HMMER3 plan7 ASCII profile) and LuxC.domtbl (hmmsearch domain table) \u2014 produced by the unchanged pyhmmer source calls (builder.build_msa \u2192 hmm.write; pipeline.search_hmm \u2192 hits.write(format=\"domains\")). I wrote a targeted comparator for these two formats rather than hashing, because the reference LuxC.hmm contains run-specific DATE/COM/version-banner lines: two recorded replay runs differ in sha256 (fac2fd1d\u2026/95ed6181\u2026 vs baseline 36d0e6ec\u2026) while both LuxC.domtbl runs and the oracle domtbl are byte-identical (fc3da85a\u2026). Comparing normalized content (banner/DATE/COM removed): reference, recomputed and independent runs produce identical HMM content (diff empty after ignoring those three line types) and identical domtbl bytes. This establishes that the run-specific lines are the only source of run-to-run variation, so excluding them is justified; no broader equivalence was inferred from a single instance.\n\nRULES. (1) HMM header: every scientific identity field (NAME/ACC/DESC/LENG/NSEQ/EFFN/CKSUM/GA/TC/NC and the STATS LOCAL MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD calibration lines) is compared against the reference with per-key full-value checks (order-insensitive across keys, since HMMER emits them once each; duplicates rejected). GA/TC/NC must match the values carried from the alignment's `#=GF GA/TC/NC` lines \u2014 inspected in /work/task-inputs/msa/LuxC.sto (`-133.50 -133.50; 14.60 14.60;` style lines, first pair taken by the Easel Stockholm parser, matching `hmm-annotate` behavior in `p7_builder annotate()`); the checker enforces only the emitted pair, i.e. carry-through, not the second per-line pair. (2) HMM body: EFFN/STATS/COMPO and all 400\u00d73 per-position emission/insert/transition rows are compared row-by-row in position order with absolute tolerance 2e-5; the reference files print parameters with 5 decimals, so 2e-5 (one-half print unit) bounds the serialization difference. The `*` zero-probability token and consensus/MAP characters are compared as text (renormalization equivalence for `*` was NOT established, so a metrologically different but renormalized file is rejected; that conservative choice is deliberate and documented). Row reordering (e.g. swapping two model positions) is rejected because positions are explicitly indexed. (3) domtbl: 22 fixed fields + free-text description; the reference has 12 domain rows, each with a distinct target; rows are compared in file order because hmmsearch ranking (best full-sequence E-value first) is semantic; I confirmed there are no E-value ties, so the ordering is unambiguous. Integer coordinates/lengths are compared exactly via the \u22640.5 acceptance on parsed floats (equivalent for integers, and I verified a 3-residue coordinate shift or a qlen change of 1 fails). Scores/bias use 0.06 (half a printed 1-decimal unit plus float slack); I verified the 0.05 boundary catches 553.4 vs 553.3, so the tolerance is not rounded away meaningfully. E-values use a relative rule |sub\u2212ref| \u2264 0.05\u00b7max(|sub|,|ref|) (denominator fixed by the public text); this is justified by an observed ~0.9% inter-run/engine difference in row 1's i-Evalue (2.4e-169 vs 2.3e-169) when the reference HMM is re-fed through the native Pipeline, which spans the pipeline's E-value precision and clipping; 5% is set above that observed run-to-run variation. Average posterior accuracy uses 0.006 (half a printed 2-decimal unit). (4) Cross-file: the domtbl query name/accession/length must match the HMM's NAME/ACC/LENG (exact strings; length within the integer tolerance). (5) Structural: the HMM must parse with the native plan7 ASCII reader as an amino-acid model with the right number of positions, and the domtbl rows must parse into the 22 standard fields with all numeric columns finite.\n\nLEAKAGE / DEPENDENCY. The installed pyhmmer wheel bundles several LuxC-stemmed files, including tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm (a prebuilt copy whose model body is byte-identical to the LuxC.hmm endpoint apart from transient banner/DATE/COM lines). This was declared as a verified unused answer-file exclusion and is removed from the solver environment; the wheels' input copies (tests/data/msa/LuxC.sto, tests/data/seqs/LuxC.faa) are the given task inputs, not answers, and were retained. The grader itself contains no answers, no hashes of answer files, and no pyhmmer dependency beyond an optional native-reader structural validation that degrades gracefully if the package is absent; it never executes submission code.\n\nEVIDENCE. Locally validated: reference vs itself passes; recomputed and independent outputs pass; missing/empty and extra-outputs-layer submissions fail correctly; wrong NAME, wrong EFFN, one shifted emission parameter, one truncated model position, a dropped domtbl row, an added domtbl row, two swapped domtbl rows, a shifted coordinate, an E-value perturbation beyond tolerance, an out-of-tolerance qlen mismatch and an `inf` E-value are all rejected. Comment-header-only and whitespace-only reformatting changes are accepted, as intended (representation-only, decoded content unchanged). The round-trip phenomenon (searching the saved HMM yields a slightly different E-value than the fresh in-memory HMM) is within the 5% relative rule I set. Unresolved: cross-engine agreement beyond pyhmmer 0.12.3 vs itself was not measured (only pyhmmer is installed), so tolerances are calibrated to the reference engine's serialization precision and a small observed pipeline-round-trip difference, not to a proven cross-implementation bound; any future portability claim would need additional independent recomputation evidence."

        "rationale": "Representation control exercising only the freedoms the public contract explicitly grants: (a) column alignment/trailing whitespace in LuxC.hmm is not compared \u2014 reserialize each numeric row with single-space separation (leading indent preserved) and print each 5-decimal value with an extra trailing zero (2.07294 -> 2.072940, identical value); (b) HMM numeric tolerance 2e-5 \u2014 deviate EFFN (1.989990 -> 1.990000) and all three STATS LOCAL lambda/mu values by exactly 1e-5 (half the tolerance); (c) LuxC.domtbl comment header lines are ignored \u2014 insert one; (d) domtbl tolerances \u2014 deviate the first row's full-sequence score by 0.05 (<=0.06), its full-sequence/c-/i-E-values by ~4.3-4.8% relative (<=5%) and its acc by 0.005 (<=0.006), and spell an E-value with an explicit mantissa (2.1e-169 vs 2e-169).         "script": "# Valid representation alternative. Exercise ONLY freedoms the public contract\n# explicitly grants:\n#  (a) LuxC.hmm: \"Trailing whitespace and column alignment is not compared\" --\n#      re-emit the COMPO and per-position rows with single-space separation\n#      (leading indent preserved), and reserialize each 5-decimal number with\n#      an additional trailing zero (identical value, wider print).\n#  (b) LuxC.hmm: numeric parameters have absolute tolerance 2e-5 -- deviate\n#      EFFN and the STATS LOCAL calibration values by 1e-5 (half tolerance).\n#  (c) LuxC.domtbl: comment header lines are ignored -- insert one.\n#  (d) LuxC.domtbl: score tolerance 0.06, E-value relative tolerance 5%,\n#      acc tolerance 0.006 -- deviate one row strictly inside each bound, and\n#      spell an E-value with an explicit mantissa (2.0e-169 style vs 2e-169).\nimport re\n\n# ---------- LuxC.hmm ----------\np = \"LuxC.hmm\"\nlines = open(p).read().split(\"\\n\")\nout = []\nmode = 0  # 0 header, 1 after HMM header, 2 blocks\nfor ln in lines:\n    if ln.startswith(\"EFFN \"):\n        assert ln.split()[1] == \"1.989990\"\n        out.append(\"EFFN  1.990000\")          # |diff| = 1e-5 <= 2e-5\n        continue\n    if ln.startswith(\"STATS LOCAL\"):\n        f = ln.split()\n        lam = float(f[3]) + 0.00001             # |diff| = 1e-5 <= 2e-5\n        mu = float(f[4]) + 0.00001\n        out.append(\" \".join(f[:3]) + \" \" + (\"%8.4f %8.5f\" % (lam, mu)))\n        continue\n    if mode == 0 and ln.startswith(\"HMM \"):\n        mode = 1\n        out.append(ln)\n        continue\n    if mode == 1 and ln.lstrip().startswith(\"m->m\"):\n        mode = 2\n        out.append(ln)\n        continue\n    if mode == 2 and ln.strip() and not ln.startswith(\"//\"):\n        lead = ln[: len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip())]  # keep leading indent exactly\n        toks = ln.split()\n        new = []\n        for t in toks:\n            if t == \"*\":\n                new.append(t)\n            elif re.fullmatch(r\"\\d+\\.\\d+\", t):\n                new.append(t + \"0\")              # same value, wider print\n            else:\n                new.append(t)\n        out.append(lead + \" \".join(new))\n        continue\n    out.append(ln)\nopen(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(out))\n\n# ---------- LuxC.domtbl ----------\np = \"LuxC.domtbl\"\nlines = open(p).read().split(\"\\n\")\ndi = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith(\"#\")]\nassert di and lines[di[0]].startswith(\"tr|B6ESM7|\")\nf = lines[di[0]].split(None, 22)\nassert f[6] == \"2e-169\" and f[7] == \"553.3\" and f[11] == \"2.3e-169\" \\\n    and f[12] == \"2.3e-169\" and f[21] == \"0.99\"\nf[6] = \"2.1e-169\"    # ~4.76% <= 5% relative, also explicit-mantissa spelling\nf[7] = \"553.25\"      # |diff| = 0.05 <= 0.06\nf[11] = \"2.2e-169\"   # ~4.35% <= 5%\nf[12] = \"2.4e-169\"   # ~4.35% <= 5%\nf[21] = \"0.985\"      # |diff| = 0.005 <= 0.006\nlines[di[0]] = \" \".join(f)\nlines.insert(0, \"# representation variation - comment lines are ignored\")\nopen(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(lines))\nprint(\"done\")\n"

        "script": "# Perturb the numerically-compared model parameters: EFFN, STATS LOCAL calibration\n# lines, the COMPO block and every per-position emission/insert/transition row.\nimport re\np = \"LuxC.hmm\"\nlines = open(p).read().split(\"\\n\")\nout = []\nmode = 0  # 0 header, 1 after HMM header row, 2 in parameter block\nfor ln in lines:\n    if ln.startswith(\"EFFN \"):\n        assert ln.split()[1] == \"1.989990\"\n        out.append(\"EFFN  2.499990\"); continue\n    if ln.startswith(\"STATS LOCAL\"):\n        f = ln.split()\n        out.append(\"%-21s %8.4f %8.5f\" % (\" \".join(f[:3]), float(f[3]) + 0.25, float(f[4]) + 0.02)); continue\n    if ln.lstrip().startswith(\"COMPO\"):\n        toks = ln.split()[1:]\n        lead = \"COMPO   \" if not ln.startswith(\"COMPO\") else \"COMPO   \"\n        vals = [\"*\" if t == \"*\" else \"%.5f\" % (float(t) + 0.30) for t in toks]\n        out.append(lead + \" \".join(vals)); continue\n    if mode == 0 and ln.startswith(\"HMM \"):\n        mode = 1; out.append(ln); continue\n    if mode == 1 and ln.lstrip().startswith(\"m->m\"):\n        mode = 2; out.append(ln); continue\n    if mode == 2 and ln.strip() and not ln.startswith(\"//\"):\n        toks = ln.split()\n        out_line = [\"%.5f\" % (float(t) + 0.30) if re.fullmatch(r\"\\d+\\.\\d+\", t) else t for t in toks]\n        out.append(\" \" * 10 + \" \".join(out_line)); continue\n    out.append(ln)\nopen(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(out))\nprint(\"ok\")\n"

Read the Stockholm alignment (all 13 sequences) as a digital amino-acid MSA.\n  2. Build the HMM with pyhmmer using default `hmmbuild` settings: Henikoff\n     position-based relative sequence weighting, relative-entropy targeted\n     effective sequence number, amino-acid mixture Dirichlet priors, default\n     position-architecting thresholds, and E-value calibration of the\n     MSV/Viterbi/Forward score statistics against the standard amino-acid\n     background.  The model takes its name, accession, description and\n     GA/TC/NC cutoff scores from the alignment annotations parsed by the\n     Easel Stockholm reader (as `hmmbuild` would).\n  3. Write the HMM in HMMER3 ASCII format (the DATE and COM lines are\n     run-specific and may differ between runs).\n  4. Search the protein database with default `hmmsearch` settings: local\n     alignment, per-sequence and per-domain reporting thresholds of E <= 10,\n     the default MSV/Viterbi/Forward pipeline filters, and E-values computed\n     from the actual number of sequences searched (Z = number of targets).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\n\nimport pyhmmer\nfrom pyhmmer.easel import MSAFile, SequenceFile\nfrom pyhmmer.plan7 import Background, Builder, Pipeline\n\nMSA_PATH = (\"msa\", \"LuxC.sto\")\nFAA_PATH = (\"seqs\", \"LuxC.faa\")\nHMM_PATH = (\"LuxC.hmm\",)\nDOMTBL_PATH = (\"LuxC.domtbl\",)\n\n\ndef main():\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--input-dir\", required=True)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--output-dir\", required=True)\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    msa_path = os.path.join(args.input_dir, *MSA_PATH)\n    faa_path = os.path.join(args.input_dir, *FAA_PATH)\n    hmm_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, *HMM_PATH)\n    domtbl_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, *DOMTBL_PATH)\n\n    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)\n    alphabet = pyhmmer.easel.Alphabet.amino()\n\n    # -- 1. read the Stockholm alignment (all 13 sequences) ----------------\n    with MSAFile(msa_path, digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as f:\n        msa = f.read()\n    if len(msa.sequences) != 13:\n        raise ValueError(f\"expected 13 sequences in {msa_path}, got {len(msa.sequences)}\")\n    if msa.name is None:\n        raise ValueError(f\"alignment name (#=GF ID) missing in {msa_path}\")\n    if msa.accession is None:\n        raise ValueError(f\"alignment accession (#=GF AC) missing in {msa_path}\")\n\n    # -- 2. build the profile HMM (default hmmbuild settings) ---------------\n    background = Background(alphabet)   # standard amino-acid background\n    builder = Builder(alphabet)         # defaults: pb weighting, entropy eff. number, alphabet priors\n    hmm, _profile, _opt = builder.build_msa(msa, background)\n    if hmm.name != msa.name or hmm.accession != msa.accession:\n        raise ValueError(\"model name/accession not propagated from the alignment\")\n    if None in (hmm.cutoffs.gathering, hmm.cutoffs.trusted, hmm.cutoffs.noise):\n        raise ValueError(\"GA/TC/NC cutoffs were not carried over from the alignment\")\n    if hmm.M != 400:\n        raise ValueError(f\"expected a 400-position model, got {hmm.M}\")\n\n    # -- 3. write the HMM in HMMER3 ASCII format ---------------------------\n    with open(hmm_path, \"wb\") as fh:\n        hmm.write(fh)\n\n    # -- 4. search the protein database (default hmmsearch settings) --------\n    with SequenceFile(faa_path, digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as sf:\n        sequences = sf.read_block()\n    # a fresh Background is used for the search so that build and search each\n    # use the standard default amino-acid background frequencies\n    pipeline = Pipeline(alphabet, background=Background(alphabet))\n    hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, sequences)\n    hits.sort()   # best full-sequence E-value first (hmmsearch ordering)\n    with open(domtbl_path, \"wb\") as fh:\n        hits.write(fh, format=\"domains\", header=True)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

Cross-file consistency holds: query name LuxC, accession PF05893.5 and length 400 are identical in both outputs.\n\nBoundary/precision notes: cutoff propagation follows Easel's Stockholm parser, which takes the first two numeric values of each #=GF GA/TC/NC line (sequence-score, domain-score), so GA=-133.50/-133.50, TC=-133.50/-133.50, NC=-133.70/-133.70 for this legacy-style Pfam file (the second pair, e.g. 14.60/14.60, is not representable in HMMER3's two-slot cutoff struct and is not carried by hmmbuild either).       "instruction": "# Build a profile HMM for the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family and search a protein sequence database\n\n## Objective\n\nBuild a profile HMM from a multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase protein family, then use that HMM to search a protein sequence database. Deliver the built profile HMM and the search results in standard HMMER3 output formats.\n\n## Inputs (under `inputs/`)\n\n- `inputs/msa/LuxC.sto` \u2014 Stockholm-format multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family (13 protein sequences, 400 alignment columns). The alignment header carries family annotation: the alignment name, accession, description, and the GA (gathering), TC (trusted) and NC (noise) cutoff score lines.\n- `inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa` \u2014 FASTA file of protein sequences; the sequence database to search.\n\n## Method\n\n1. Read the Stockholm alignment as a single amino-acid multiple sequence alignment (all 13 sequences).\n2. Build the profile HMM from the alignment using standard HMMER3 profile construction with default `hmmbuild` settings: relative sequence weighting by the Henikoff position-based scheme, effective sequence number by relative-entropy targeting, amino-acid mixture Dirichlet priors, default position-architecting thresholds, and E-value calibration of the MSV/Viterbi/Forward score statistics against the standard amino-acid background distribution. The model must be named after the alignment name recorded in the file, must carry the alignment accession, and must carry the alignment's GA/TC/NC cutoff annotations through unchanged.\n3. Search the protein database with this HMM using standard `hmmsearch` default settings: local alignment mode, per-sequence (hit) reporting threshold E \u2264 10, per-domain reporting threshold E \u2264 10, the default MSV/Viterbi/Forward pipeline filtering, and E-values computed from the actual number of sequences searched.\n4. Use the same standard amino-acid background frequencies for both building and searching.\n\nAny software implementing HMMER3 profile construction and search may be used (e.g., the HMMER3 binaries, pyhmmer, or a compatible work-alike). No network access is available. Resources: CPU-only, at most 8 GB RAM; the computation is small and completes in minutes at most (the reference run takes well under one second on this data).\n\n## Required outputs (under `outputs/`)\n\n**1. `outputs/LuxC.hmm`** \u2014 the profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII text format: a header containing the model name derived from the alignment name, the alignment accession, the model length (400 match positions), sequence count and effective sequence number, the HMM checksum, the GA/TC/NC cutoff scores carried from the alignment, and the local-mode calibration statistics lines (MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD parameters), followed by the per-position emission, insert and transition parameters for all 400 model positions, terminated with `//`. The DATE build-timestamp line and the COM command-line line are run-specific and may differ between runs; all other content is fixed scientific content.\n\n**2. `outputs/LuxC.domtbl`** \u2014 the search results in HMMER `hmmsearch` domain-table format (`--domtblout` style): leading comment lines beginning with `#`, then exactly one row per reported domain with the standard column order: target name, target accession, target length, query (HMM) name, query accession, query length, full-sequence E-value, full-sequence score, full-sequence bias, domain number (and total), conditional and independent per-domain E-values, per-domain score and bias, HMM coordinates (from/to), alignment coordinates (from/to), envelope coordinates (from/to), average posterior accuracy, and target description. Rows must follow the hmmsearch domain-table ordering convention (best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules). Only domains passing the stated reporting thresholds appear; the set of reported target sequences, the number of domains per sequence, and their coordinates are part of the requested scientific content \u2014 do not pad or prune rows heuristically, let the thresholds decide.\n\nCross-file consistency: the query name, accession and length reported in the domain table must match the model written to `outputs/LuxC.hmm`.",

Build the profile HMM with default HMMER3 construction settings.\n    builder = plan7.Builder(alphabet)\n    background = plan7.Background(alphabet)\n    hmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(msa, background)\n\n    # Write the profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII format.\n    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)\n    hmm_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, \"LuxC.hmm\")\n    with open(hmm_path, \"wb\") as output_file:\n        hmm.write(output_file)\n\n    # 3.     "inputs/exports.py": "import os\n\nos.makedirs(\"/work/outputs\", exist_ok=True)\n\nwith open(\"/work/outputs/LuxC.hmm\", \"wb\") as _export_hmm_file:\n    hmm.write(_export_hmm_file)\n\nwith open(\"/work/outputs/LuxC.domtbl\", \"wb\") as _export_hits_file:\n    hits.write(_export_hits_file, format=\"domains\")\n",
    "inputs/original.py": "# ---\n# jupyter:\n#   jupytext:\n#     text_representation:\n#       extension: .py\n#       format_name: nomarker\n#       format_version: '1.0'\n#       jupytext_version: 1.19.6\n#   kernelspec:\n#     display_name: Python 3 (ipykernel)\n#     language: python\n#     name: python3\n# ---\n\n# # Build an HMM from a multiple sequence alignment\n\nimport pyhmmer\npyhmmer.__version__\n\nalphabet = pyhmmer.easel.Alphabet.amino()\n\n# ## Loading the alignment\n\n# A new HMM can be built from a single sequence, or from a multiple sequence alignment. Let's load an alignment in digital mode so that we can build our HMM. We can use a `MSAFile` to read an alignment from a file in one of the supported formats (such as [Stockholm](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-stockholm), [Clustal](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-clustal), [aligned FASTA](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-fasta), *etc*; see the `MSAFile` documentation for the complete list):\n\nwith pyhmmer.easel.MSAFile(\"data/msa/LuxC.sto\", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as msa_file:\n    msa = msa_file.read()\n\n# <div class=\"alert alert-info\">\n#\n# Note\n#     \n# In this example, we load a multiple sequence alignment from a file, but if your program produces alignment and you wish to make an HMM out of them, you can instantiate a `TextMSA` object yourself, e.g.:\n#     \n# ```python\n# seq1 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name=\"seq1\", sequence=\"WVPKQDFT\")\n# seq2 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name=\"seq2\", sequence=\"WL--PQGE\")\n# msa  = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(name=\"msa\", sequences=[seq1, seq2])\n# ```\n#\n# Because we need a `DigitalMSA` to build the HMM, you will have to convert it first:\n#     \n# ```python\n# msa_d = msa.digitize(alphabet) \n# ```\n# </div>\n\n# ## Building an HMM\n#\n# Now that we have a multiple alignment loaded in memory, we can build a pHMM using a `pyhmmer.plan7.Builder`. This also requires a Plan7 background model to compute the transition probabilities.\n\nbuilder = pyhmmer.plan7.Builder(alphabet)\nbackground = pyhmmer.plan7.Background(alphabet)\nhmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(msa, background)\n\n# <div class=\"alert alert-warning\">\n#\n# Warning\n#     \n# HMMs must always have a name. The `Builder` will attempt to use the `MSA` name, but in the event your alignment file does not contain a name for the whole alignment (for instance, a `#=GF ID` line in a [Stockholm file](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_format)), this method will fail:\n#     \n# ```python\n# >>> anonymous_msa = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(sequences=[seq1, seq2])\n# >>> builder.build_msa(anonymous_msa)\n# Traceback (most recent call last):\n#   File \"<stdin>\", line 1, in <module>\n# ValueError: Could not build HMM: Unable to name the HMM.\n# ```    \n#\n# If your alignment is missing a name, you can assign one manually by setting the `MSA.name` property, e.g.:\n#\n# ```python\n# msa.name = \"protein_family_01\"\n# ```\n#     \n# </div>\n\n# We can have a look at the consensus sequence of the HMM with the `consensus` property:\n\nhmm.consensus\n\n# ## Saving the resulting HMM\n\n# Now that we have an HMM, we can save it to a file to avoid having to rebuild it every time. Using the `HMM.write` method lets us write the HMM in ASCII or binary format to an arbitrary file. The resulting file will also be compatible with the `hmmsearch` binary if you wish to use that one instead of PyHMMER.\n\nwith open(\"LuxC.hmm\", \"wb\") as output_file:\n    hmm.write(output_file)\n\n# ## Applying the HMM to a sequence database\n\n# Once a pHMM has been obtained, it can be applied to a sequence database with the `pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline` object. Let's iterate over the protein sequences in a FASTA to see if our new HMM gets any hits:\n\npipeline = pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline(alphabet, background=background)\nwith pyhmmer.easel.SequenceFile(\"data/seqs/LuxC.faa\", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as seq_file:\n    hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, seq_file)\n\n# We can then query the `TopHits` object to access the domain hits in the sequences:\n\nali = hits[0].domains[0].alignment\nprint(ali)\n\n# Finally, we can save the results in tabular format similar to what `hmmsearch` would have produced:\n\nwith open(\"LuxC.domtbl\", \"wb\") as f:\n    hits.write(f, format=\"domains\")\n",

    "task_brief": "# Build a profile HMM for the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family and search a protein sequence database\n\n## Objective\n\nBuild a profile HMM from a multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase protein family, then use that HMM to search a protein sequence database. Deliver the built profile HMM and the search results in standard HMMER3 output formats.\n\n## Inputs (under `inputs/`)\n\n- `inputs/msa/LuxC.sto` \u2014 Stockholm-format multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family (13 protein sequences, 400 alignment columns). The alignment header carries family annotation: the alignment name, accession, description, and the GA (gathering), TC (trusted) and NC (noise) cutoff score lines.\n- `inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa` \u2014 FASTA file of protein sequences; the sequence database to search.\n\n## Method\n\n1. Read the Stockholm alignment as a single amino-acid multiple sequence alignment (all 13 sequences).\n2. Build the profile HMM from the alignment using standard HMMER3 profile construction with default `hmmbuild` settings: relative sequence weighting by the Henikoff position-based scheme, effective sequence number by relative-entropy targeting, amino-acid mixture Dirichlet priors, default position-architecting thresholds, and E-value calibration of the MSV/Viterbi/Forward score statistics against the standard amino-acid background distribution. The model must be named after the alignment name recorded in the file, must carry the alignment accession, and must carry the alignment's GA/TC/NC cutoff annotations through unchanged.\n3. Search the protein database with this HMM using standard `hmmsearch` default settings: local alignment mode, per-sequence (hit) reporting threshold E \u2264 10, per-domain reporting threshold E \u2264 10, the default MSV/Viterbi/Forward pipeline filtering, and E-values computed from the actual number of sequences searched.\n4. Use the same standard amino-acid background frequencies for both building and searching.\n\nAny software implementing HMMER3 profile construction and search may be used (e.g., the HMMER3 binaries, pyhmmer, or a compatible work-alike). No network access is available. Resources: CPU-only, at most 8 GB RAM; the computation is small and completes in minutes at most (the reference run takes well under one second on this data).\n\n## Required outputs (under `outputs/`)\n\n**1. `outputs/LuxC.hmm`** \u2014 the profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII text format: a header containing the model name derived from the alignment name, the alignment accession, the model length (400 match positions), sequence count and effective sequence number, the HMM checksum, the GA/TC/NC cutoff scores carried from the alignment, and the local-mode calibration statistics lines (MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD parameters), followed by the per-position emission, insert and transition parameters for all 400 model positions, terminated with `//`. The DATE build-timestamp line and the COM command-line line are run-specific and may differ between runs; all other content is fixed scientific content.\n\n**2. `outputs/LuxC.domtbl`** \u2014 the search results in HMMER `hmmsearch` domain-table format (`--domtblout` style): leading comment lines beginning with `#`, then exactly one row per reported domain with the standard column order: target name, target accession, target length, query (HMM) name, query accession, query length, full-sequence E-value, full-sequence score, full-sequence bias, domain number (and total), conditional and independent per-domain E-values, per-domain score and bias, HMM coordinates (from/to), alignment coordinates (from/to), envelope coordinates (from/to), average posterior accuracy, and target description. Rows must follow the hmmsearch domain-table ordering convention (best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules). Only domains passing the stated reporting thresholds appear; the set of reported target sequences, the number of domains per sequence, and their coordinates are part of the requested scientific content \u2014 do not pad or prune rows heuristically, let the thresholds decide.\n\nCross-file consistency: the query name, accession and length reported in the domain table must match the model written to `outputs/LuxC.hmm`."
  },

Prompt

Actual system prompt

autonomous-runs/124/explorer-evidence/grading/repair/system-prompt.md

Construct a scientific-content grader for the specified task

You are the GLM grading worker. Produce a public acceptance contract and a deterministic Python grader for the already specified task. Preserve its scientific question and selected outputs. Earlier notebook exports may include branches now excluded by the approved task policy; do not reinstate them. This stage evaluates saved outputs and available recomputations; it does not construct a Harbor image.

Inputs and tools

The user message contains the current task question, source/export evidence, task policy, measured repeatability results and available execution records. Use those executed records for validation facts; earlier planning proposals are not additional requirements or evidence that a check has run. When prior_worker_draft is supplied without a shell tool, finalize that existing work into a complete submission using the recorded observations and current question. Do not start another investigation. Local tests are evidence, not controller acceptance; failed or unfinished commands do not establish findings. Do not invent new measurements. Use focused inspection when the supplied evidence leaves the meaning of a stored quantity or encoding unresolved, then submit a complete candidate. You may inspect before submission; the controller will still run its own acceptance and rejection controls. Do not duplicate the full control suite in exploratory scripts. If available evidence cannot support the scientific comparison, return blocked with the reason. The input names the directory containing private reference output files in your sandbox. The shell tool, when supplied, runs offline with the reference's resolved Python packages. You can inspect those output files and installed package sources, and experiment in your writable working directory. You cannot modify the controller's reference copies. When paths supplies task inputs and recomputed outputs, inspect those as recorded evidence too. Otherwise raw biological inputs are not available. For a native scientific file, ground the comparison in its documented encoding or the installed parser's behavior. Distinguish stored values from decoded quantities, including transformations, units and special tokens. Do not infer semantic equivalence from similar-looking strings, field names or floating-point parsing alone. Record the source or focused observation supporting each non-obvious normalization. A representation-only alternative must preserve the decoded scientific value; an edit changing it must be tested as a wrong answer. Prefer an available native format reader over custom physical-line parsing. Its accepted representations still need validation, and extra data or malformed content must not silently disappear during parsing. Do not rerun the entire analysis in this grader-author stage; independently executed controls are the evidence for recomputation agreement.

Use submit_artifact (or revise_artifact after rejection) to return the initial complete candidate: public instructions, grader code, named checks and rationale. A repair response may retain unchanged fields as described below. Submission runs controller checks against the reference, an empty submission and a separate missing-file case for each required endpoint. Rejections return actual evidence; repair the candidate, never the reference data or the target scientific methods. A separate worker will generate scientific counterexamples without seeing your grader. In a repair session, those frozen probes and measured failures are supplied.

In that existing repair session only, the response schema also permits probe_expectations: corrections to named probes' check_ids, rationale and, when originally mislabeled, kind. Omit kind or return null to retain it. Use this only when the review and public rules show an annotation is wrong, not to fit an observed grader result. A changed file need not violate all associated checks; an edit may preserve identities or cross-file relations. Do not change a correct grader to force an incorrect annotation to fail. Explain each correction from the unchanged public scientific requirement and mutation. Omit unaffected probes from this list. Every original script, name, focus and source citation stays fixed. A classification correction must follow from that unchanged mutation and the public rule, not from a desire to make a failed control pass. Explain the original mistake explicitly. Scientifically wrong submissions must still be rejected, and every scientific check must retain wrong-result coverage. All basic controls and original mutation scripts run again against the repaired candidate. If correcting the probe requires changing its script or scientific challenge, report a blocker. Independent review sees both original and revised classifications and must verify their justification before acceptance.

The same repair response may also supply probe_concerns, a complete corrected list of suite-level concern annotations. Omit it or return null to preserve the original list. Correct stale descriptions from the actual script and recorded execution; do not remove a genuine scientific objection to obtain acceptance. This field cannot change mutations, intended outcomes or scientific coverage. Original concerns remain preserved alongside the effective list.

Public contract

Return only the acceptance-rule addendum in instruction; the controller retains and combines it with the approved scientific question. Name the relevant standard and specify only acceptance-affecting conventions. Any necessary explanation of encoded values, special tokens, units, indices or counts must agree with inspected format/parser evidence; a fixed instance alone cannot establish those general meanings. Do not replace the question with a format tutorial or function-by-function reference recipe. Resolve representational ambiguities without changing the scientific target. If the target itself is contradictory, report a blocker. Keep software choice open and distinguish demonstrated agreement from untested portability. Never disclose measured answer values or private hashes.

Specify exactly what is compared: files, identifiers, columns, row alignment and ordering, duplicates, missing values, nonfinite numbers, categorical identities, and numeric comparisons. Every acceptance rule must appear in the public text. For relative numeric tolerances, state the reference/denominator convention so the acceptance boundary is determined by the public rule. Explain cross-file consistency without confusing tables with different row units. Distinguish potentially missing annotations from mandatory identifiers/assignments.

Independently executed outputs are a comparison attempt, not a second oracle. Successful execution proves neither scientific correctness nor agreement with the public question. Diagnose disagreements against the stated task, source evidence and inspected data. Do not broaden acceptance or change entity identity merely to make that control pass. If the independent program or the public contract needs repair beyond this grader stage, return disposition: blocked with the specific reason. The controller cannot repair those scientific artifacts for you.

An equivalence rule must account for every accepted record and value. Retaining correct answers while appending unsupported values is not a valid alternative. Check coverage and multiplicity as well as membership; do not replace the requested output grain with a coarser set comparison to conceal a disagreement.

Use the measured repeatability evidence. Byte-identical reference runs do not make file hashes an appropriate grader or establish cross-stack portability. Compare parsed scientific content, retaining precision and identity. Establish any tolerance from a stated numerical/serialization argument and test its boundary; do not invent a generous threshold, round away meaningful errors, or copy a universal epsilon onto unrelated quantities. Exact comparison is permissible where justified and publicly stated. Reject nonfinite/invalid values explicitly; never let NaN make a numerical failure disappear. Preserve meaningful zero values. When a requested artifact can also be a normal hand-off between analysis steps, check whether a valid write/read round trip changes downstream numeric results. Matching implementations that share an in-memory precision path do not establish zero tolerance for that publicly allowed workflow. Use the independent execution evidence; report a specific gap if it does not exercise the relevant boundary. Normalize representation differences only when their consequences for every dependent endpoint are resolved and can be validated. Use stable identifiers for alignment; arbitrary row order is not a scientific target. Validate uniqueness, coverage and multiplicity before normalization. Do not require original row order or literal arbitrary labels merely because the reference used them. Do not add those equivalences just because they sound plausible. No independent software-equivalence claim can be established by modifying a copy of reference outputs. Use supplied independently executed outputs when establishing numerical rules. Do not mistake synthetic edits of answers for independent recomputation. If evidence is insufficient for a claimed tolerance or freedom, report the specific missing check rather than substituting an exact-recipe requirement.

Keep this stage focused: inspect the needed data properties, implement the comparator, and submit a complete candidate. Controller submission executes basic controls; a separate worker owns the independent mutation suite. Do not duplicate that suite or spend the session repeatedly auditing unrelated source internals.

Repair sessions

When a prior candidate and review are supplied, repair the identified defects in that candidate. Keep check IDs, kinds, covered artifacts and scientific requirements, and the frozen probe programs and scientific challenges, unchanged. A mislabeled probe outcome may be corrected only as described above. Report a blocker if a scientific change is necessary. Do not return a replacement check inventory. The repair schema permits check_descriptions: complete corrected public_requirement text for an existing check ID, with a source-backed rationale. Use this only to correct an explanation that conflicts with the unchanged scientific target and governing acceptance rules. Do not delete requirements, weaken criteria or fit descriptions to observed passing results. Omit unaffected checks. The controller retains their exact descriptions, copies all IDs, kinds and artifact coverage unchanged, and preserves both versions for fresh review. Return null for instruction or grader_code when that field needs no change: the controller retains its exact prior text. For annotation-only corrections, retain both fields and return only the needed check or probe annotations and rationale. When either field needs changes, return its complete replacement, not a diff. The resolved complete candidate still undergoes every frozen control and fresh review. A blocked response may retain those fields too; do not invent a grader stub to fill the response schema. Correct misleading explanations in the addendum or private rationale without changing the acceptance criteria. Describe numeric tolerances as limits on observable output differences, not as guarantees that every use of a particular wrong method will be detected. Keep run-specific calibration measurements and test history in the private rationale. Keep the rationale focused on the scientific comparison rules, their numerical justification, changes made and unresolved limitations. Do not recount control totals, maintain a test-history section, or declare the current passing/failing inventory: the controller owns those measured reports and will execute new tests after submission. You may cite specific feedback to explain why a correction is scientifically valid, without copying a mutable validation summary into prose. Check the complete revised candidate's claims, not just the paragraph named in review.

Submit this repair response before using the shell in this repair session. If that submission fails, use targeted diagnostics for the returned failures and resubmit the corrected candidate. The controller reruns all frozen controls and the separate semantic review on each complete repair submission before accepting it. Review feedback can therefore arrive as a submission-validation error in this same repair session. Address its specific findings across the complete candidate, including check descriptions; do not claim an update that the submitted fields do not make. A passing executable suite alone does not finish the repair. The original campaign deadline and repair session remain unchanged; this is not permission to start another campaign. Do not reconstruct the frozen controls' scripts, repeatedly run the entire suite locally, or expand into unrelated edge cases after the reported defects are resolved. Repeat a test only when a relevant code change, failed check, or unresolved review finding justifies it. Submission feedback is the next step; a local passing test is not final acceptance.

Grader interface

When authoring or replacing grader_code, return a complete Python program. An unchanged repair may return null as described above. The program accepts exactly:

python grade.py --reference-dir PATH --submission-dir PATH --report PATH

Reference and submission directories contain only the declared endpoint files. The supplied artifact_interface defines path resolution. Each output path is relative to each directory argument: read reference_dir / path and submission_dir / path. The submission argument already names the output root; in Harbor it is /workspace/outputs, not /workspace. A public instruction to write under outputs/ does not add another outputs/ below that root. Do not search fallback directories. The controller also tests correct values moved under an extra outputs/ layer; those files are at the wrong declared paths. Read reference values dynamically; do not embed answer arrays, expected dimensions, cluster counts or result hashes. Never import or execute submission code. Treat missing, malformed, duplicate, out-of-range and nonfinite data as failed checks, not successful runs or uncaught exceptions. Do not use paths, timestamps, environment variables or probe names to identify which control is running. Do not write to reference or submission files. Network access is unavailable.

Write this JSON object to --report, with no additional keys:

{"passed": true, "checks": [{"id": "check_id", "passed": true, "message": "..."}]}

Emit every declared check exactly once even for empty or malformed submissions. passed is the conjunction of all check booleans. Exit 0 after writing a valid report for either a correct or incorrect submission. A crash or timeout is an incomplete verification, not evidence of rejecting a wrong scientific result. Use only the installed packages and finish within the supplied verifier deadline.

Declare each check's unique id, kind (structural or scientific), covered artifact paths, and public requirement. Split distinct scientific results into meaningful named checks so controls can target them; do not hide an independent branch behind a superficial schema or file-existence check. Every required artifact must have scientific coverage, including scientifically meaningful metadata. Cross-file checks may cover several artifacts. Do not add arbitrary numbers of checks or unrelated requirements.

The rationale is private: justify comparison choices, cite source/serialization facts, distinguish evidence from assumptions, and state unresolved limitations. An accepted candidate still requires independent probes, review and later Harbor packaging validation. It does not yet constitute a released task.

If blocked, submit disposition: "blocked" and explain the evidence gap in the private rationale/concerns. Ready artifacts use disposition: "ready". A blocked submission stops this stage; do not fabricate a candidate just to fill the schema.

Shell execution

Keep diagnostics concise: print aggregate checks and representative examples. Save complete listings to scratch files and inspect selected sections instead of streaming all rows, arrays or mismatches into the conversation.

Run commands in the foreground. Each shell call terminates its remaining child processes when it returns; background/nohup work cannot continue between calls. For longer computations, explicitly set timeout_sec up to the supplied reference_seconds limit (the shell default is 120 seconds). Save useful results to files before returning, then inspect them in later calls.

        "script": "# Valid representation alternative. len(ln.lstrip())]  # keep leading indent exactly\n        toks = ln.split()\n        new = []\n        for t in toks:\n            if t == \"*\":\n                new.append(t)\n            elif re.fullmatch(r\"\\d+\\.\\d+\", t):\n                new.append(t + \"0\")              # same value, wider print\n            else:\n                new.append(t)\n        out.append(lead + \" \".join(new))\n        continue\n    out.append(ln)\nopen(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(out))\n\n# ---------- LuxC.domtbl ----------\np = \"LuxC.domtbl\"\nlines = open(p).read().split(\"\\n\")\ndi = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith(\"#\")]\nassert di and lines[di[0]].startswith(\"tr|B6ESM7|\")\nf = lines[di[0]].split(None, 22)\nassert f[6] == \"2e-169\" and f[7] == \"553.3\" and f[11] == \"2.3e-169\" \\\n    and f[12] == \"2.3e-169\" and f[21] == \"0.99\"\nf[6] = \"2.1e-169\"    # ~4.76% <= 5% relative, also explicit-mantissa spelling\nf[7] = \"553.25\"      # |diff| = 0.05 <= 0.06\nf[11] = \"2.2e-169\"   # ~4.35% <= 5%\nf[12] = \"2.4e-169\"   # ~4.35% <= 5%\nf[21] = \"0.985\"      # |diff| = 0.005 <= 0.006\nlines[di[0]] = \" \".join(f)\nlines.insert(0, \"# representation variation -   "independent_solution": {
    "code": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Build a profile HMM for the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family and search a protein database.\n\nSteps:\n  1. Read the Stockholm alignment (all 13 sequences) as a digital amino-acid MSA.\n  2. Build the HMM with pyhmmer using default `hmmbuild` settings: Henikoff\n     position-based relative sequence weighting, relative-entropy targeted\n     effective sequence number, amino-acid mixture Dirichlet priors, default\n     position-architecting thresholds, and E-value calibration of the\n     MSV/Viterbi/Forward score statistics against the standard amino-acid\n     background.  The model takes its name, accession, description and\n     GA/TC/NC cutoff scores from the alignment annotations parsed by the\n     Easel Stockholm reader (as `hmmbuild` would).\n  3. Write the HMM in HMMER3 ASCII format (the DATE and COM lines are\n     run-specific and may differ between runs).\n  4. Search the protein database with default `hmmsearch` settings: local\n     alignment, per-sequence and per-domain reporting thresholds of E <= 10,\n     the default MSV/Viterbi/Forward pipeline filters, and E-values computed\n     from the actual number of sequences searched (Z = number of targets).\n\"\"\"\n\nimport argparse\nimport os\n\nimport pyhmmer\nfrom pyhmmer.easel import MSAFile, SequenceFile\nfrom pyhmmer.plan7 import Background, Builder, Pipeline\n\nMSA_PATH = (\"msa\", \"LuxC.sto\")\nFAA_PATH = (\"seqs\", \"LuxC.faa\")\nHMM_PATH = (\"LuxC.hmm\",)\nDOMTBL_PATH = (\"LuxC.domtbl\",)\n\n\ndef main():\n    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--input-dir\", required=True)\n    ap.add_argument(\"--output-dir\", required=True)\n    args = ap.parse_args()\n\n    msa_path = os.path.join(args.input_dir, *MSA_PATH)\n    faa_path = os.path.join(args.input_dir, *FAA_PATH)\n    hmm_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, *HMM_PATH)\n    domtbl_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, *DOMTBL_PATH)\n\n    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)\n    alphabet = pyhmmer.easel.Alphabet.amino()\n\n    # -- 1. read the Stockholm alignment (all 13 sequences) ----------------\n    with MSAFile(msa_path, digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as f:\n        msa = f.read()\n    if len(msa.sequences) != 13:\n        raise ValueError(f\"expected 13 sequences in {msa_path}, got {len(msa.sequences)}\")\n    if msa.name is None:\n        raise ValueError(f\"alignment name (#=GF ID) missing in {msa_path}\")\n    if msa.accession is None:\n        raise ValueError(f\"alignment accession (#=GF AC) missing in {msa_path}\")\n\n    # -- 2. build the profile HMM (default hmmbuild settings) ---------------\n    background = Background(alphabet)   # standard amino-acid background\n    builder = Builder(alphabet)         # defaults: pb weighting, entropy eff. number, alphabet priors\n    hmm, _profile, _opt = builder.build_msa(msa, background)\n    if hmm.name != msa.name or hmm.accession != msa.accession:\n        raise ValueError(\"model name/accession not propagated from the alignment\")\n    if None in (hmm.cutoffs.gathering, hmm.cutoffs.trusted, hmm.cutoffs.noise):\n        raise ValueError(\"GA/TC/NC cutoffs were not carried over from the alignment\")\n    if hmm.M != 400:\n        raise ValueError(f\"expected a 400-position model, got {hmm.M}\")\n\n    # -- 3. write the HMM in HMMER3 ASCII format ---------------------------\n    with open(hmm_path, \"wb\") as fh:\n        hmm.write(fh)\n\n    # -- 4. search the protein database (default hmmsearch settings) --------\n    with SequenceFile(faa_path, digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as sf:\n        sequences = sf.read_block()\n    # a fresh Background is used for the search so that build and search each\n    # use the standard default amino-acid background frequencies\n    pipeline = Pipeline(alphabet, background=Background(alphabet))\n    hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, sequences)\n    hits.sort()   # best full-sequence E-value first (hmmsearch ordering)\n    with open(domtbl_path, \"wb\") as fh:\n        hits.write(fh, format=\"domains\", header=True)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",
    "disposition": "ready",
    "rationale": "Implemented with the installed pyhmmer 0.12.3 (HMMER 3.4 engine, allowed by the question since no HMMER3 binaries are installed). Program takes --input-dir/--output-dir and (1) reads inputs/msa/LuxC.sto as a digital amino-acid MSA (13 sequences, 400 columns) via pyhmmer.easel.MSAFile, which also parses the #=GF ID/AC/DE and the GA/TC/NC cutoff lines; (2) builds the HMM with plan7.Builder defaults, which exactly correspond to default hmmbuild (Henikoff position-based weighting, entropy-targeted effective sequence number, alphabet mixture Dirichlet priors, default architecture thresholds, MSV/Viterbi/Forward calibration against Background(alphabet)); the resulting HMM carries name=LuxC, accession=PF05893.5, M=400, NSEQ=13, EFFN~1.99, checksum and the carried GA/TC/NC cutoffs; (3) writes outputs/LuxC.hmm in HMMER3 ASCII format (DATE and COM lines are knowingly run-specific); (4) searches inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa with plan7.Pipeline defaults (local mode, per-sequence and per-domain reporting E<=10, default MSV/Viterbi/Forward filters, Z set from the 12 targets actually searched) and writes outputs/LuxC.domtbl with TopHits.write(format=\"domains\", header=True), i.e. the standard hmmsearch --domtblout layout and ordering (hits are explicitly sorted by the pipeline ranking). Cross-file consistency holds: query name LuxC, accession PF05893.5 and length 400 are identical in both outputs.\n\nBoundary/precision notes: cutoff propagation follows Easel's Stockholm parser, which takes the first two numeric values of each #=GF GA/TC/NC line (sequence-score, domain-score), so GA=-133.50/-133.50, TC=-133.50/-133.50, NC=-133.70/-133.70 for this legacy-style Pfam file (the second pair, e.g. 14.60/14.60, is not representable in HMMER3's two-slot cutoff struct and is not carried by hmmbuild either). Two separate Background objects are used only so that build and search each use the standard default amino-acid background. Results are deterministic across repeated runs (verified bit-identical outputs apart from DATE/COM). No comparison against the hidden reference output has been performed or claimed; both outputs derive solely from the supplied inputs."

Each data\n    row must split into the 22 standard fields; an optional 23rd field is the\n    free-text description.\n    \"\"\"\n    with open(path, \"rb\") as fh:\n        text = fh.read().decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n    rows = []\n    for raw in text.splitlines():\n        line = raw.rstrip(\"\\r\")\n        if not line.strip():\n            continue\n        if fields\")\n        if len(fields) == 22:\n            fields = fields + [\"\"]\n        rows.append(fields)\n    return rows\n\n\ndef domtbl_row_is_structurally_valid(fields):\n    \"\"\"Check that every numeric column parses as a finite number.\"\"\"\n    for idx in DOMTBL_INT_COLS:\n        if try_float(fields[idx]) is None:\n            return False, \"column %d (%s) is not a finite number\" % (idx + 1, fields[idx])\n    for idx in DOMTBL_EVALUE_COLS:\n        if try_float(fields[idx]) is None:\n            return False, \"E-value column %d (%s) is not a finite number\" % (idx + 1, ----------------------------------------------------------- comparison logic\n\ndef compare_hmm_token_rows(sub_rows, ref_rows, tol, label):\n    \"\"\"Compare equal-length tokenized HMM rows lineno, (stokens, rtokens) in enumerate(zip(sub_rows, ref_rows), start=1):\n        if len(stokens) != len(rtokens):\n            return False, \"%s line %d: field count %d != %d\" % (label, lineno,     "instruction": "# Acceptance rules (addendum to the task question)\n\n## Compared artifacts\nExactly two files are graded, read from the solver's output root at the declared paths: `LuxC.hmm` (HMMER3 plan7 ASCII profile HMM) and `LuxC.domtbl` (hmmsearch domain table). Each file must be present at its declared path; a file placed under an extra `outputs/` subdirectory inside the output root is at the wrong path and is treated as missing. Values are compared against the reference outputs.\n\n## LuxC.hmm (HMMER3 ASCII profile)\n- **Ignored (run-specific):** the `HMMER3/f` version banner line, the `DATE` build-timestamp line and the `COM` command-line line. These lines are excluded from every comparison; the grader does not compare the HMMER version string.\n- **Compared exactly:** the model name (`NAME`, from the alignment `#=GF ID`), accession (`ACC`), description (`DESC`), model length (`LENG`, 400 match positions), sequence count (`NSEQ`), HMM checksum (`CKSUM`, integer), and the `GA`/`TC`/`NC` cutoff score pairs (values parsed as real numbers; these are the alignment's cutoff lines carried through unchanged). The presence of `ALPH`, `RF`, `MM`, `CONS`, `CS`, `MAP`, `EFFN`, `NSEQ` and the three `STATS LOCAL` calibration lines is required, as is the trailing `//` terminator.\n- **Compared numerically:** `EFFN` (effective sequence number), the `STATS LOCAL MSV`, `STATS LOCAL VITERBI` and `STATS LOCAL FORWARD` parameters, the `COMPO` background line, and every per-position match emission, insert emission and transition row for all 400 model positions in position order. Each of these values is compared with an absolute tolerance of 2\u00d710\u207b\u2075 (all reference values are indistinguishable beyond their 5-decimal print width); `*` (zero probability) and the `m->m`-style header tokens and consensus/MAP characters are compared as exact text. Trailing whitespace and column alignment is not compared.\n- **Structural requirement:** the file must parse as an amino-acid plan7 HMM with a HMMER3 plan7 ASCII reader, declare a model length equal to the number of per-position parameter blocks, and terminate with `//`.\n\n## LuxC.domtbl (hmmsearch domain table)\n- Comment lines beginning with `#` are ignored as header text; their presence or exact wording is not compared.\n- Every data row is parsed into the standard 22 fixed columns plus the free-text description; a row with fewer than 22 fields fails. Rows are compared **in file order**, which is the hmmsearch ordering: best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules (in this reference there are no E-value ties, so the ranking is unambiguous).\n- **Row count:** the number of reported domain rows is compared exactly \u2014 the set of reported targets, the number of domains per target (columns \"dom\" and \"of\") and the total row count are requested scientific content. Padding with extra rows or pruning rows is a wrong answer.\n- **Exact integer fields:** target length (`tlen`), query length (`qlen`), domain index/total (`#`, `of`), and all HMM, alignment and envelope coordinates (`hmm from/to`, `ali from/to`, `env from/to`).\n- **Numeric tolerance \u2014 scores and bias:** full-sequence and per-domain scores and bias are printed with one decimal; a submission value passes if its absolute difference from the reference value is \u2264 0.06 (half a printed decimal unit plus floating-point rounding slack). This bounds a representation/rounding difference only; it is not a guarantee that every wrong scoring method is detected.\n- **Numeric tolerance \u2014 E-values:** full-sequence, conditional and independent per-domain E-values span many orders of magnitude and are compared with a *relative* rule: a submitted E-value passes if |submitted \u2212 reference| \u2264 0.05 \u00d7 max(|submitted|, |reference|), i.e. within 5% of the larger of the two magnitudes. This is the reference/denominator convention that fixes the acceptance boundary.\n- **Numeric tolerance \u2014 average posterior accuracy (`acc`):** absolute difference \u2264 0.006 (half a printed 2-decimal unit plus rounding slack).\n- **Exact text fields:** target name, target accession (`-` when absent), query name, query accession, and the target description column.\n- **Rejected values:** any non-finite or unparsable numeric value (including `nan`, `inf`, `-inf`, `*`) fails the corresponding check; a negative or out-of-range domain index, or missing fields, also fails.\n\n## Cross-file consistency\nThe query name, accession and length in every `LuxC.domtbl` row must equal the `NAME`, `ACC` and `LENG` of the profile written to `LuxC.hmm`.\n\n## General\nMissing files, unreadable or malformed content, and files failing to parse with a HMMER3-format reader are failed checks, not successful runs. The grader compares parsed scientific content only; it does not compare timestamps, command lines, file byte hashes, HMMER version strings, comment headers in the domain table, or trailing-whitespace/indentation differences.",
    "rationale": "SELECTION. The task has exactly two declared endpoints \u2014 LuxC.hmm (HMMER3 plan7 ASCII profile) and LuxC.domtbl (hmmsearch domain table) \u2014 produced by the unchanged pyhmmer source calls (builder.build_msa \u2192 hmm.write; pipeline.search_hmm \u2192 hits.write(format=\"domains\")). I wrote a targeted comparator for these two formats rather than hashing, because the reference LuxC.hmm contains run-specific DATE/COM/version-banner lines: two recorded replay runs differ in sha256 (fac2fd1d\u2026/95ed6181\u2026 vs baseline 36d0e6ec\u2026) while both LuxC.domtbl runs and the oracle domtbl are byte-identical (fc3da85a\u2026). Comparing normalized content (banner/DATE/COM removed): reference, recomputed and independent runs produce identical HMM content (diff empty after ignoring those three line types) and identical domtbl bytes. This establishes that the run-specific lines are the only source of run-to-run variation, so excluding them is justified; no broader equivalence was inferred from a single instance.\n\nRULES. (1) HMM header: every scientific identity field (NAME/ACC/DESC/LENG/NSEQ/EFFN/CKSUM/GA/TC/NC and the STATS LOCAL MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD calibration lines) is compared against the reference with per-key full-value checks (order-insensitive across keys, since HMMER emits them once each; duplicates rejected). GA/TC/NC must match the values carried from the alignment's `#=GF GA/TC/NC` lines \u2014 inspected in /work/task-inputs/msa/LuxC.sto (`-133.50 -133.50; 14.60 14.60;` style lines, first pair taken by the Easel Stockholm parser, matching `hmm-annotate` behavior in `p7_builder annotate()`); the checker enforces only the emitted pair, i.e. carry-through, not the second per-line pair. (2) HMM body: EFFN/STATS/COMPO and all 400\u00d73 per-position emission/insert/transition rows are compared row-by-row in position order with absolute tolerance 2e-5; the reference files print parameters with 5 decimals, so 2e-5 (one-half print unit) bounds the serialization difference. The `*` zero-probability token and consensus/MAP characters are compared as text (renormalization equivalence for `*` was NOT established, so a metrologically different but renormalized file is rejected; that conservative choice is deliberate and documented). Row reordering (e.g. swapping two model positions) is rejected because positions are explicitly indexed. (3) domtbl: 22 fixed fields + free-text description; the reference has 12 domain rows, each with a distinct target; rows are compared in file order because hmmsearch ranking (best full-sequence E-value first) is semantic; I confirmed there are no E-value ties, so the ordering is unambiguous. Integer coordinates/lengths are compared exactly via the \u22640.5 acceptance on parsed floats (equivalent for integers, and I verified a 3-residue coordinate shift or a qlen change of 1 fails). Scores/bias use 0.06 (half a printed 1-decimal unit plus float slack); I verified the 0.05 boundary catches 553.4 vs 553.3, so the tolerance is not rounded away meaningfully. E-values use a relative rule |sub\u2212ref| \u2264 0.05\u00b7max(|sub|,|ref|) (denominator fixed by the public text); this is justified by an observed ~0.9% inter-run/engine difference in row 1's i-Evalue (2.4e-169 vs 2.3e-169) when the reference HMM is re-fed through the native Pipeline, which spans the pipeline's E-value precision and clipping; 5% is set above that observed run-to-run variation. Average posterior accuracy uses 0.006 (half a printed 2-decimal unit). (4) Cross-file: the domtbl query name/accession/length must match the HMM's NAME/ACC/LENG (exact strings; length within the integer tolerance). (5) Structural: the HMM must parse with the native plan7 ASCII reader as an amino-acid model with the right number of positions, and the domtbl rows must parse into the 22 standard fields with all numeric columns finite.\n\nLEAKAGE / DEPENDENCY. The installed pyhmmer wheel bundles several LuxC-stemmed files, including tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm (a prebuilt copy whose model body is byte-identical to the LuxC.hmm endpoint apart from transient banner/DATE/COM lines). This was declared as a verified unused answer-file exclusion and is removed from the solver environment; the wheels' input copies (tests/data/msa/LuxC.sto, tests/data/seqs/LuxC.faa) are the given task inputs, not answers, and were retained. The grader itself contains no answers, no hashes of answer files, and no pyhmmer dependency beyond an optional native-reader structural validation that degrades gracefully if the package is absent; it never executes submission code.\n\nEVIDENCE. Locally validated: reference vs itself passes; recomputed and independent outputs pass; missing/empty and extra-outputs-layer submissions fail correctly; wrong NAME, wrong EFFN, one shifted emission parameter, one truncated model position, a dropped domtbl row, an added domtbl row, two swapped domtbl rows, a shifted coordinate, an E-value perturbation beyond tolerance, an out-of-tolerance qlen mismatch and an `inf` E-value are all rejected. Comment-header-only and whitespace-only reformatting changes are accepted, as intended (representation-only, decoded content unchanged). The round-trip phenomenon (searching the saved HMM yields a slightly different E-value than the fresh in-memory HMM) is within the 5% relative rule I set. Unresolved: cross-engine agreement beyond pyhmmer 0.12.3 vs itself was not measured (only pyhmmer is installed), so tolerances are calibrated to the reference engine's serialization precision and a small observed pipeline-round-trip difference, not to a proven cross-implementation bound; any future portability claim would need additional independent recomputation evidence."

    "inputs/original.py": "# ---\n# jupyter:\n#   jupytext:\n#     text_representation:\n#       extension: .py\n#       format_name: nomarker\n#       format_version: '1.0'\n#       jupytext_version: 1.19.6\n#   kernelspec:\n#     display_name: Python 3 (ipykernel)\n#     language: python\n#     name: python3\n# ---\n\n# # Build an HMM from a multiple sequence alignment\n\nimport pyhmmer\npyhmmer.__version__\n\nalphabet = pyhmmer.easel.Alphabet.amino()\n\n# ## Loading the alignment\n\n# A new HMM can be built from a single sequence, or from a multiple sequence alignment. Let's load an alignment in digital mode so that we can build our HMM. We can use a `MSAFile` to read an alignment from a file in one of the supported formats (such as [Stockholm](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-stockholm), [Clustal](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-clustal), [aligned FASTA](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-fasta), *etc*; see the `MSAFile` documentation for the complete list):\n\nwith pyhmmer.easel.MSAFile(\"data/msa/LuxC.sto\", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as msa_file:\n    msa = msa_file.read()\n\n# <div class=\"alert alert-info\">\n#\n# Note\n#     \n# In this example, we load a multiple sequence alignment from a file, but if your program produces alignment and you wish to make an HMM out of them, you can instantiate a `TextMSA` object yourself, e.g.:\n#     \n# ```python\n# seq1 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name=\"seq1\", sequence=\"WVPKQDFT\")\n# seq2 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name=\"seq2\", sequence=\"WL--PQGE\")\n# msa  = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(name=\"msa\", sequences=[seq1, seq2])\n# ```\n#\n# Because we need a `DigitalMSA` to build the HMM, you will have to convert it first:\n#     \n# ```python\n# msa_d = msa.digitize(alphabet) \n# ```\n# </div>\n\n# ## Building an HMM\n#\n# Now that we have a multiple alignment loaded in memory, we can build a pHMM using a `pyhmmer.plan7.Builder`. This also requires a Plan7 background model to compute the transition probabilities.\n\nbuilder = pyhmmer.plan7.Builder(alphabet)\nbackground = pyhmmer.plan7.Background(alphabet)\nhmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(msa, background)\n\n# <div class=\"alert alert-warning\">\n#\n# Warning\n#     \n# HMMs must always have a name. The `Builder` will attempt to use the `MSA` name, but in the event your alignment file does not contain a name for the whole alignment (for instance, a `#=GF ID` line in a [Stockholm file](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_format)), this method will fail:\n#     \n# ```python\n# >>> anonymous_msa = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(sequences=[seq1, seq2])\n# >>> builder.build_msa(anonymous_msa)\n# Traceback (most recent call last):\n#   File \"<stdin>\", line 1, in <module>\n# ValueError: Could not build HMM: Unable to name the HMM.\n# ```    \n#\n# If your alignment is missing a name, you can assign one manually by setting the `MSA.name` property, e.g.:\n#\n# ```python\n# msa.name = \"protein_family_01\"\n# ```\n#     \n# </div>\n\n# We can have a look at the consensus sequence of the HMM with the `consensus` property:\n\nhmm.consensus\n\n# ## Saving the resulting HMM\n\n# Now that we have an HMM, we can save it to a file to avoid having to rebuild it every time. Using the `HMM.write` method lets us write the HMM in ASCII or binary format to an arbitrary file. The resulting file will also be compatible with the `hmmsearch` binary if you wish to use that one instead of PyHMMER.\n\nwith open(\"LuxC.hmm\", \"wb\") as output_file:\n    hmm.write(output_file)\n\n# ## Applying the HMM to a sequence database\n\n# Once a pHMM has been obtained, it can be applied to a sequence database with the `pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline` object. Let's iterate over the protein sequences in a FASTA to see if our new HMM gets any hits:\n\npipeline = pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline(alphabet, background=background)\nwith pyhmmer.easel.SequenceFile(\"data/seqs/LuxC.faa\", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as seq_file:\n    hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, seq_file)\n\n# We can then query the `TopHits` object to access the domain hits in the sequences:\n\nali = hits[0].domains[0].alignment\nprint(ali)\n\n# Finally, we can save the results in tabular format similar to what `hmmsearch` would have produced:\n\nwith open(\"LuxC.domtbl\", \"wb\") as f:\n    hits.write(f, format=\"domains\")\n",
