      "instruction": "# Build a profile HMM for the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family and search a protein sequence database\n\n## Objective\n\nBuild a profile HMM from a multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase protein family, then use that HMM to search a protein sequence database. Deliver the built profile HMM and the search results in standard HMMER3 output formats.\n\n## Inputs (under `inputs/`)\n\n- `inputs/msa/LuxC.sto` \u2014 Stockholm-format multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family (13 protein sequences, 400 alignment columns). The alignment header carries family annotation: the alignment name, accession, description, and the GA (gathering), TC (trusted) and NC (noise) cutoff score lines.\n- `inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa` \u2014 FASTA file of protein sequences; the sequence database to search.\n\n## Method\n\n1. Read the Stockholm alignment as a single amino-acid multiple sequence alignment (all 13 sequences).\n2. Build the profile HMM from the alignment using standard HMMER3 profile construction with default `hmmbuild` settings: relative sequence weighting by the Henikoff position-based scheme, effective sequence number by relative-entropy targeting, amino-acid mixture Dirichlet priors, default position-architecting thresholds, and E-value calibration of the MSV/Viterbi/Forward score statistics against the standard amino-acid background distribution. The model must be named after the alignment name recorded in the file, must carry the alignment accession, and must carry the alignment's GA/TC/NC cutoff annotations through unchanged.\n3. Search the protein database with this HMM using standard `hmmsearch` default settings: local alignment mode, per-sequence (hit) reporting threshold E \u2264 10, per-domain reporting threshold E \u2264 10, the default MSV/Viterbi/Forward pipeline filtering, and E-values computed from the actual number of sequences searched.\n4. Use the same standard amino-acid background frequencies for both building and searching.\n\nAny software implementing HMMER3 profile construction and search may be used (e.g., the HMMER3 binaries, pyhmmer, or a compatible work-alike). No network access is available. Resources: CPU-only, at most 8 GB RAM; the computation is small and completes in minutes at most (the reference run takes well under one second on this data).\n\n## Required outputs (under `outputs/`)\n\n**1. `outputs/LuxC.hmm`** \u2014 the profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII text format: a header containing the model name derived from the alignment name, the alignment accession, the model length (400 match positions), sequence count and effective sequence number, the HMM checksum, the GA/TC/NC cutoff scores carried from the alignment, and the local-mode calibration statistics lines (MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD parameters), followed by the per-position emission, insert and transition parameters for all 400 model positions, terminated with `//`. The DATE build-timestamp line and the COM command-line line are run-specific and may differ between runs; all other content is fixed scientific content.\n\n**2. `outputs/LuxC.domtbl`** \u2014 the search results in HMMER `hmmsearch` domain-table format (`--domtblout` style): leading comment lines beginning with `#`, then exactly one row per reported domain with the standard column order: target name, target accession, target length, query (HMM) name, query accession, query length, full-sequence E-value, full-sequence score, full-sequence bias, domain number (and total), conditional and independent per-domain E-values, per-domain score and bias, HMM coordinates (from/to), alignment coordinates (from/to), envelope coordinates (from/to), average posterior accuracy, and target description. Rows must follow the hmmsearch domain-table ordering convention (best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules). Only domains passing the stated reporting thresholds appear; the set of reported target sequences, the number of domains per sequence, and their coordinates are part of the requested scientific content \u2014 do not pad or prune rows heuristically, let the thresholds decide.\n\nCross-file consistency: the query name, accession and length reported in the domain table must match the model written to `outputs/LuxC.hmm`.",

      "oracle_code": "import argparse\nimport os\n\n\ndef locate(root, rel):\n    \"\"\"Locate a required input file relative to the given input root.\"\"\"\n    for cand in (os.path.join(root, rel), os.path.join(root, \"inputs\", rel)):\n        if os.path.exists(cand):\n            return cand\n    raise FileNotFoundError(f\"required input {rel!r} not found under {root}\")\n\n\ndef main():\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Build the LuxC profile HMM and search the protein database\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--input-dir\", required=True, help=\"Directory containing the supplied inputs\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--output-dir\", required=True, help=\"Directory to write the required outputs\")\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n\n    import pyhmmer\n    from pyhmmer import easel, plan7\n\n    # Amino-acid alphabet used for reading, building, and searching.\n    alphabet = easel.Alphabet.amino()\n\n    # 1. Read the Stockholm alignment as one digital amino-acid MSA.\n    msa_path = locate(args.input_dir, \"msa/LuxC.sto\")\n    with easel.MSAFile(msa_path, digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as msa_file:\n        msa = msa_file.read()\n\n    # 2. Build the profile HMM with default HMMER3 construction settings.\n    builder = plan7.Builder(alphabet)\n    background = plan7.Background(alphabet)\n    hmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(msa, background)\n\n    # Write the profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII format.\n    os.makedirs(args.output_dir, exist_ok=True)\n    hmm_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, \"LuxC.hmm\")\n    with open(hmm_path, \"wb\") as output_file:\n        hmm.write(output_file)\n\n    # 3. Search the protein sequence database with the built HMM,\n    #    using hmmsearch defaults (local mode, E<=10 / domE<=10 thresholds,\n    #    default MSV/Viterbi/Forward filtering, Z from the sequence count).\n    pipeline = plan7.Pipeline(alphabet, background=background)\n    seq_path = locate(args.input_dir, \"seqs/LuxC.faa\")\n    with easel.SequenceFile(seq_path, digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as seq_file:\n        hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, seq_file)\n\n    # Write the search hits in hmmsearch domain-table format.\n    domtbl_path = os.path.join(args.output_dir, \"LuxC.domtbl\")\n    with open(domtbl_path, \"wb\") as f:\n        hits.write(f, format=\"domains\")\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n",

This is a tolerance-rule weakness, not an ambiguity I could resolve from the files.",

If even single-space packing were rejected by the actual reader, the valid-alternative probe could fail for representation-only reasons \u2014 the remaining freedoms exercised (numeric-within-tolerance, comment insertion, mantissa spelling) are explicitly permitted by text."

  "source_evidence": {
    "candidate/dependency-exclusions.json": "{\n  \"files\": [\n    {\n      \"distribution\": \"pyhmmer\",\n      \"path\": \"pyhmmer/tests/data/hmms/txt/LuxC.hmm\",\n      \"sha256\": \"e7a4dd57c83fb17cc12640f20c4f02f126d8230b16d6c6ef596bf791c8075865\",\n      \"reason\": \"Bundled test-data copy of the precomputed LuxC profile HMM from the pyhmmer test suite. Its HMM-model body (1204 emitted model lines, 1,115 non-annotation lines after the transient DATE/COM/HMMER3-version header) is byte-identical to the LuxC.hmm artifact this task requires the solver to rebuild from LuxC.sto, so keeping it would expose a near-complete precomputed answer. The analysis never imports or reads it: the imported modules are pyhmmer.easel and pyhmmer.plan7 only, the script builds its own HMM from /inputs/msa/LuxC.sto, and the file is a packaged test fixture, not library code.\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n",
    "candidate/pyproject.toml": "[project]\nname = \"pyhmmer-msa-to-hmm-setup\"\nversion = \"0.1.0\"\nrequires-python = \">=3.13\"\ndependencies = [\n  \"pyhmmer==0.12.3\",\n]\n",
    "inputs/exports.py": "import os\n\nos.makedirs(\"/work/outputs\", exist_ok=True)\n\nwith open(\"/work/outputs/LuxC.hmm\", \"wb\") as _export_hmm_file:\n    hmm.write(_export_hmm_file)\n\nwith open(\"/work/outputs/LuxC.domtbl\", \"wb\") as _export_hits_file:\n    hits.write(_export_hits_file, format=\"domains\")\n",
    "inputs/original.py": "# ---\n# jupyter:\n#   jupytext:\n#     text_representation:\n#       extension: .py\n#       format_name: nomarker\n#       format_version: '1.0'\n#       jupytext_version: 1.19.6\n#   kernelspec:\n#     display_name: Python 3 (ipykernel)\n#     language: python\n#     name: python3\n# ---\n\n# # Build an HMM from a multiple sequence alignment\n\nimport pyhmmer\npyhmmer.__version__\n\nalphabet = pyhmmer.easel.Alphabet.amino()\n\n# ## Loading the alignment\n\n# A new HMM can be built from a single sequence, or from a multiple sequence alignment. Let's load an alignment in digital mode so that we can build our HMM. We can use a `MSAFile` to read an alignment from a file in one of the supported formats (such as [Stockholm](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-stockholm), [Clustal](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-clustal), [aligned FASTA](https://www.tbi.univie.ac.at/RNA/ViennaRNA/doc/html/file_formats.html#msa-formats-fasta), *etc*; see the `MSAFile` documentation for the complete list):\n\nwith pyhmmer.easel.MSAFile(\"data/msa/LuxC.sto\", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as msa_file:\n    msa = msa_file.read()\n\n# <div class=\"alert alert-info\">\n#\n# Note\n#     \n# In this example, we load a multiple sequence alignment from a file, but if your program produces alignment and you wish to make an HMM out of them, you can instantiate a `TextMSA` object yourself, e.g.:\n#     \n# ```python\n# seq1 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name=\"seq1\", sequence=\"WVPKQDFT\")\n# seq2 = pyhmmer.easel.TextSequence(name=\"seq2\", sequence=\"WL--PQGE\")\n# msa  = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(name=\"msa\", sequences=[seq1, seq2])\n# ```\n#\n# Because we need a `DigitalMSA` to build the HMM, you will have to convert it first:\n#     \n# ```python\n# msa_d = msa.digitize(alphabet) \n# ```\n# </div>\n\n# ## Building an HMM\n#\n# Now that we have a multiple alignment loaded in memory, we can build a pHMM using a `pyhmmer.plan7.Builder`. This also requires a Plan7 background model to compute the transition probabilities.\n\nbuilder = pyhmmer.plan7.Builder(alphabet)\nbackground = pyhmmer.plan7.Background(alphabet)\nhmm, _, _ = builder.build_msa(msa, background)\n\n# <div class=\"alert alert-warning\">\n#\n# Warning\n#     \n# HMMs must always have a name. The `Builder` will attempt to use the `MSA` name, but in the event your alignment file does not contain a name for the whole alignment (for instance, a `#=GF ID` line in a [Stockholm file](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stockholm_format)), this method will fail:\n#     \n# ```python\n# >>> anonymous_msa = pyhmmer.easel.TextMSA(sequences=[seq1, seq2])\n# >>> builder.build_msa(anonymous_msa)\n# Traceback (most recent call last):\n#   File \"<stdin>\", line 1, in <module>\n# ValueError: Could not build HMM: Unable to name the HMM.\n# ```    \n#\n# If your alignment is missing a name, you can assign one manually by setting the `MSA.name` property, e.g.:\n#\n# ```python\n# msa.name = \"protein_family_01\"\n# ```\n#     \n# </div>\n\n# We can have a look at the consensus sequence of the HMM with the `consensus` property:\n\nhmm.consensus\n\n# ## Saving the resulting HMM\n\n# Now that we have an HMM, we can save it to a file to avoid having to rebuild it every time. Using the `HMM.write` method lets us write the HMM in ASCII or binary format to an arbitrary file. The resulting file will also be compatible with the `hmmsearch` binary if you wish to use that one instead of PyHMMER.\n\nwith open(\"LuxC.hmm\", \"wb\") as output_file:\n    hmm.write(output_file)\n\n# ## Applying the HMM to a sequence database\n\n# Once a pHMM has been obtained, it can be applied to a sequence database with the `pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline` object. Let's iterate over the protein sequences in a FASTA to see if our new HMM gets any hits:\n\npipeline = pyhmmer.plan7.Pipeline(alphabet, background=background)\nwith pyhmmer.easel.SequenceFile(\"data/seqs/LuxC.faa\", digital=True, alphabet=alphabet) as seq_file:\n    hits = pipeline.search_hmm(hmm, seq_file)\n\n# We can then query the `TopHits` object to access the domain hits in the sequences:\n\nali = hits[0].domains[0].alignment\nprint(ali)\n\n# Finally, we can save the results in tabular format similar to what `hmmsearch` would have produced:\n\nwith open(\"LuxC.domtbl\", \"wb\") as f:\n    hits.write(f, format=\"domains\")\n",

  "specification": {
    "task_brief": "# Build a profile HMM for the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family and search a protein sequence database\n\n## Objective\n\nBuild a profile HMM from a multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase protein family, then use that HMM to search a protein sequence database. Deliver the built profile HMM and the search results in standard HMMER3 output formats.\n\n## Inputs (under `inputs/`)\n\n- `inputs/msa/LuxC.sto` \u2014 Stockholm-format multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family (13 protein sequences, 400 alignment columns). The alignment header carries family annotation: the alignment name, accession, description, and the GA (gathering), TC (trusted) and NC (noise) cutoff score lines.\n- `inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa` \u2014 FASTA file of protein sequences; the sequence database to search.\n\n## Method\n\n1. Read the Stockholm alignment as a single amino-acid multiple sequence alignment (all 13 sequences).\n2. Build the profile HMM from the alignment using standard HMMER3 profile construction with default `hmmbuild` settings: relative sequence weighting by the Henikoff position-based scheme, effective sequence number by relative-entropy targeting, amino-acid mixture Dirichlet priors, default position-architecting thresholds, and E-value calibration of the MSV/Viterbi/Forward score statistics against the standard amino-acid background distribution. The model must be named after the alignment name recorded in the file, must carry the alignment accession, and must carry the alignment's GA/TC/NC cutoff annotations through unchanged.\n3. Search the protein database with this HMM using standard `hmmsearch` default settings: local alignment mode, per-sequence (hit) reporting threshold E \u2264 10, per-domain reporting threshold E \u2264 10, the default MSV/Viterbi/Forward pipeline filtering, and E-values computed from the actual number of sequences searched.\n4. Use the same standard amino-acid background frequencies for both building and searching.\n\nAny software implementing HMMER3 profile construction and search may be used (e.g., the HMMER3 binaries, pyhmmer, or a compatible work-alike). No network access is available. Resources: CPU-only, at most 8 GB RAM; the computation is small and completes in minutes at most (the reference run takes well under one second on this data).\n\n## Required outputs (under `outputs/`)\n\n**1. `outputs/LuxC.hmm`** \u2014 the profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII text format: a header containing the model name derived from the alignment name, the alignment accession, the model length (400 match positions), sequence count and effective sequence number, the HMM checksum, the GA/TC/NC cutoff scores carried from the alignment, and the local-mode calibration statistics lines (MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD parameters), followed by the per-position emission, insert and transition parameters for all 400 model positions, terminated with `//`. The DATE build-timestamp line and the COM command-line line are run-specific and may differ between runs; all other content is fixed scientific content.\n\n**2. `outputs/LuxC.domtbl`** \u2014 the search results in HMMER `hmmsearch` domain-table format (`--domtblout` style): leading comment lines beginning with `#`, then exactly one row per reported domain with the standard column order: target name, target accession, target length, query (HMM) name, query accession, query length, full-sequence E-value, full-sequence score, full-sequence bias, domain number (and total), conditional and independent per-domain E-values, per-domain score and bias, HMM coordinates (from/to), alignment coordinates (from/to), envelope coordinates (from/to), average posterior accuracy, and target description. Rows must follow the hmmsearch domain-table ordering convention (best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules). Only domains passing the stated reporting thresholds appear; the set of reported target sequences, the number of domains per sequence, and their coordinates are part of the requested scientific content \u2014 do not pad or prune rows heuristically, let the thresholds decide.\n\nCross-file consistency: the query name, accession and length reported in the domain table must match the model written to `outputs/LuxC.hmm`."
  },

      "name": "val-repr-permitted-freedoms",
      "rationale": "Representation control exercising only the freedoms the public contract explicitly grants: (a) column alignment/trailing whitespace in LuxC.hmm is not compared \u2014 reserialize each numeric row with single-space separation (leading indent preserved) and print each 5-decimal value with an extra trailing zero (2.07294 -> 2.072940, identical value); (b) HMM numeric tolerance 2e-5 \u2014 deviate EFFN (1.989990 -> 1.990000) and all three STATS LOCAL lambda/mu values by exactly 1e-5 (half the tolerance); (c) LuxC.domtbl comment header lines are ignored \u2014 insert one; (d) domtbl tolerances \u2014 deviate the first row's full-sequence score by 0.05 (<=0.06), its full-sequence/c-/i-E-values by ~4.3-4.8% relative (<=5%) and its acc by 0.005 (<=0.006), and spell an E-value with an explicit mantissa (2.1e-169 vs 2e-169). Every changed value stays strictly inside the published tolerance bounds, so all checks must pass. The dominant application-relevant use of these tolerances is the fixed-width decimal serialization of HMMER values; this probe does not attempt any recomputation.",
      "script": "# Valid representation alternative. Exercise ONLY freedoms the public contract\n# explicitly grants:\n#  (a) LuxC.hmm: \"Trailing whitespace and column alignment is not compared\" --\n#      re-emit the COMPO and per-position rows with single-space separation\n#      (leading indent preserved), and reserialize each 5-decimal number with\n#      an additional trailing zero (identical value, wider print).\n#  (b) LuxC.hmm: numeric parameters have absolute tolerance 2e-5 -- deviate\n#      EFFN and the STATS LOCAL calibration values by 1e-5 (half tolerance).\n#  (c) LuxC.domtbl: comment header lines are ignored -- insert one.\n#  (d) LuxC.domtbl: score tolerance 0.06, E-value relative tolerance 5%,\n#      acc tolerance 0.006 -- deviate one row strictly inside each bound, and\n#      spell an E-value with an explicit mantissa (2.0e-169 style vs 2e-169).\nimport re\n\n# ---------- LuxC.hmm ----------\np = \"LuxC.hmm\"\nlines = open(p).read().split(\"\\n\")\nout = []\nmode = 0  # 0 header, 1 after HMM header, 2 blocks\nfor ln in lines:\n    if ln.startswith(\"EFFN \"):\n        assert ln.split()[1] == \"1.989990\"\n        out.append(\"EFFN  1.990000\")          # |diff| = 1e-5 <= 2e-5\n        continue\n    if ln.startswith(\"STATS LOCAL\"):\n        f = ln.split()\n        lam = float(f[3]) + 0.00001             # |diff| = 1e-5 <= 2e-5\n        mu = float(f[4]) + 0.00001\n        out.append(\" \".join(f[:3]) + \" \" + (\"%8.4f %8.5f\" % (lam, mu)))\n        continue\n    if mode == 0 and ln.startswith(\"HMM \"):\n        mode = 1\n        out.append(ln)\n        continue\n    if mode == 1 and ln.lstrip().startswith(\"m->m\"):\n        mode = 2\n        out.append(ln)\n        continue\n    if mode == 2 and ln.strip() and not ln.startswith(\"//\"):\n        lead = ln[: len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip())]  # keep leading indent exactly\n        toks = ln.split()\n        new = []\n        for t in toks:\n            if t == \"*\":\n                new.append(t)\n            elif re.fullmatch(r\"\\d+\\.\\d+\", t):\n                new.append(t + \"0\")              # same value, wider print\n            else:\n                new.append(t)\n        out.append(lead + \" \".join(new))\n        continue\n    out.append(ln)\nopen(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(out))\n\n# ---------- LuxC.domtbl ----------\np = \"LuxC.domtbl\"\nlines = open(p).read().split(\"\\n\")\ndi = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith(\"#\")]\nassert di and lines[di[0]].startswith(\"tr|B6ESM7|\")\nf = lines[di[0]].split(None, 22)\nassert f[6] == \"2e-169\" and f[7] == \"553.3\" and f[11] == \"2.3e-169\" \\\n    and f[12] == \"2.3e-169\" and f[21] == \"0.99\"\nf[6] = \"2.1e-169\"    # ~4.76% <= 5% relative, also explicit-mantissa spelling\nf[7] = \"553.25\"      # |diff| = 0.05 <= 0.06\nf[11] = \"2.2e-169\"   # ~4.35% <= 5%\nf[12] = \"2.4e-169\"   # ~4.35% <= 5%\nf[21] = \"0.985\"      # |diff| = 0.005 <= 0.006\nlines[di[0]] = \" \".join(f)\nlines.insert(0, \"# representation variation - comment lines are ignored\")\nopen(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(lines))\nprint(\"done\")\n"
    }

autonomous-runs/124/explorer-evidence/native/solver-input.md

You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{ "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?", "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.", "commands": [ { "keystrokes": "ls -la\n", "duration": 0.1 }, { "keystrokes": "cd project\n", "duration": 0.1 } ], "task_complete": true }

Required fields:

  • "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
  • "plan": Your plan for the next steps
  • "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:

  • "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:

  • "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
  • "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:

  • You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
  • For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
    • C-c for Ctrl+C
    • C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:

  • Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
  • Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
  • Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
  • The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
  • Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:

Build a profile HMM for the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family and search a protein sequence database

Objective

Build a profile HMM from a multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase protein family, then use that HMM to search a protein sequence database. Deliver the built profile HMM and the search results in standard HMMER3 output formats.

Inputs (under inputs/)

  • inputs/msa/LuxC.sto — Stockholm-format multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC acyl-CoA reductase family (13 protein sequences, 400 alignment columns). The alignment header carries family annotation: the alignment name, accession, description, and the GA (gathering), TC (trusted) and NC (noise) cutoff score lines.
  • inputs/seqs/LuxC.faa — FASTA file of protein sequences; the sequence database to search.

Method

  1. Read the Stockholm alignment as a single amino-acid multiple sequence alignment (all 13 sequences).
  2. Build the profile HMM from the alignment using standard HMMER3 profile construction with default hmmbuild settings: relative sequence weighting by the Henikoff position-based scheme, effective sequence number by relative-entropy targeting, amino-acid mixture Dirichlet priors, default position-architecting thresholds, and E-value calibration of the MSV/Viterbi/Forward score statistics against the standard amino-acid background distribution. The model must be named after the alignment name recorded in the file, must carry the alignment accession, and must carry the alignment's GA/TC/NC cutoff annotations through unchanged.
  3. Search the protein database with this HMM using standard hmmsearch default settings: local alignment mode, per-sequence (hit) reporting threshold E ≤ 10, per-domain reporting threshold E ≤ 10, the default MSV/Viterbi/Forward pipeline filtering, and E-values computed from the actual number of sequences searched.
  4. Use the same standard amino-acid background frequencies for both building and searching.

Any software implementing HMMER3 profile construction and search may be used (e.g., the HMMER3 binaries, pyhmmer, or a compatible work-alike). No network access is available. Resources: CPU-only, at most 8 GB RAM; the computation is small and completes in minutes at most (the reference run takes well under one second on this data).

Required outputs (under outputs/)

1. outputs/LuxC.hmm — the profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII text format: a header containing the model name derived from the alignment name, the alignment accession, the model length (400 match positions), sequence count and effective sequence number, the HMM checksum, the GA/TC/NC cutoff scores carried from the alignment, and the local-mode calibration statistics lines (MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD parameters), followed by the per-position emission, insert and transition parameters for all 400 model positions, terminated with //. The DATE build-timestamp line and the COM command-line line are run-specific and may differ between runs; all other content is fixed scientific content.

2. outputs/LuxC.domtbl — the search results in HMMER hmmsearch domain-table format (--domtblout style): leading comment lines beginning with #, then exactly one row per reported domain with the standard column order: target name, target accession, target length, query (HMM) name, query accession, query length, full-sequence E-value, full-sequence score, full-sequence bias, domain number (and total), conditional and independent per-domain E-values, per-domain score and bias, HMM coordinates (from/to), alignment coordinates (from/to), envelope coordinates (from/to), average posterior accuracy, and target description. Rows must follow the hmmsearch domain-table ordering convention (best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules). Only domains passing the stated reporting thresholds appear; the set of reported target sequences, the number of domains per sequence, and their coordinates are part of the requested scientific content — do not pad or prune rows heuristically, let the thresholds decide.

Cross-file consistency: the query name, accession and length reported in the domain table must match the model written to outputs/LuxC.hmm.

Acceptance rules

Acceptance rules (addendum to the task question)

Compared artifacts

Exactly two files are graded, read from the solver's output root at the declared paths: LuxC.hmm (HMMER3 plan7 ASCII profile HMM) and LuxC.domtbl (hmmsearch domain table). Each file must be present at its declared path; a file placed under an extra outputs/ subdirectory inside the output root is at the wrong path and is treated as missing. Values are compared against the reference outputs.

LuxC.hmm (HMMER3 ASCII profile)

  • Ignored (run-specific): the HMMER3/f version banner line, the DATE build-timestamp line and the COM command-line line. These lines are excluded from every comparison; the grader does not compare the HMMER version string.
  • Compared exactly: the model name (NAME, from the alignment #=GF ID), accession (ACC), description (DESC), model length (LENG, 400 match positions), sequence count (NSEQ), HMM checksum (CKSUM, integer), and the GA/TC/NC cutoff score pairs (values parsed as real numbers; these are the alignment's cutoff lines carried through unchanged). The presence of ALPH, RF, MM, CONS, CS, MAP, EFFN, NSEQ and the three STATS LOCAL calibration lines is required, as is the trailing // terminator.
  • Compared numerically: EFFN (effective sequence number), the STATS LOCAL MSV, STATS LOCAL VITERBI and STATS LOCAL FORWARD parameters, the COMPO background line, and every per-position match emission, insert emission and transition row for all 400 model positions in position order. Each of these values is compared with an absolute tolerance of 2×10⁻⁵ (all reference values are indistinguishable beyond their 5-decimal print width); * (zero probability) and the m->m-style header tokens and consensus/MAP characters are compared as exact text. Trailing whitespace and column alignment is not compared.
  • Structural requirement: the file must parse as an amino-acid plan7 HMM with a HMMER3 plan7 ASCII reader, declare a model length equal to the number of per-position parameter blocks, and terminate with //.

LuxC.domtbl (hmmsearch domain table)

  • Comment lines beginning with # are ignored as header text; their presence or exact wording is not compared.
  • Every data row is parsed into the standard 22 fixed columns plus the free-text description; a row with fewer than 22 fields fails. Rows are compared in file order, which is the hmmsearch ordering: best full-sequence E-value first, with the hmmsearch tie-break rules (in this reference there are no E-value ties, so the ranking is unambiguous).
  • Row count: the number of reported domain rows is compared exactly — the set of reported targets, the number of domains per target (columns "dom" and "of") and the total row count are requested scientific content. Padding with extra rows or pruning rows is a wrong answer.
  • Exact integer fields: target length (tlen), query length (qlen), domain index/total (#, of), and all HMM, alignment and envelope coordinates (hmm from/to, ali from/to, env from/to).
  • Numeric tolerance — scores and bias: full-sequence and per-domain scores and bias are printed with one decimal; a submission value passes if its absolute difference from the reference value is ≤ 0.06 (half a printed decimal unit plus floating-point rounding slack). This bounds a representation/rounding difference only; it is not a guarantee that every wrong scoring method is detected.
  • Numeric tolerance — E-values: full-sequence, conditional and independent per-domain E-values span many orders of magnitude and are compared with a relative rule: a submitted E-value passes if |submitted − reference| ≤ 0.05 × max(|submitted|, |reference|), i.e. within 5% of the larger of the two magnitudes. This is the reference/denominator convention that fixes the acceptance boundary.
  • Numeric tolerance — average posterior accuracy (acc): absolute difference ≤ 0.006 (half a printed 2-decimal unit plus rounding slack).
  • Exact text fields: target name, target accession (- when absent), query name, query accession, and the target description column.
  • Rejected values: any non-finite or unparsable numeric value (including nan, inf, -inf, *) fails the corresponding check; a negative or out-of-range domain index, or missing fields, also fails.

Cross-file consistency

The query name, accession and length in every LuxC.domtbl row must equal the NAME, ACC and LENG of the profile written to LuxC.hmm.

General

Missing files, unreadable or malformed content, and files failing to parse with a HMMER3-format reader are failed checks, not successful runs. The grader compares parsed scientific content only; it does not compare timestamps, command lines, file byte hashes, HMMER version strings, comment headers in the domain table, or trailing-whitespace/indentation differences.

Task directories

Read the supplied inputs from /workspace/inputs/. Write all required output files under /workspace/outputs/, using the relative filenames specified above. The working directory is /workspace. Aliases /inputs/ and /outputs/ refer to these same directories.

repo:experiments/19-repo2rlenv-notebook-pilot/stage_scientific_release.py

"""Operator release staging from accepted native evidence; never edits task science."""

import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from release_metadata import (
    load_release_metadata,
    release_execution_provenance,
    scientific_probe_documents,
    verify_bundle_licenses,
)
from repo2rlenv.campaigns.release import ReleasePlan, ReleaseTask, stage_release, verify_release
from repo2rlenv.emitter.evaluation import EvaluationLabel, evaluation_time
from repo2rlenv.quality.labels import write_labeled_copy

config_path = Path(sys.argv[1])
config = json.loads(config_path.read_text())

"""Publish an inspected release into the authenticated user's public namespace."""

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from huggingface_hub import HfApi, hf_hub_download
from huggingface_hub.errors import EntryNotFoundError, RepositoryNotFoundError
from repo2rlenv.campaigns.release import publish_release, verify_release


class SerialHfApi(HfApi):
    """The SDK exposes upload concurrency on create_commit, not upload_folder."""

    def create_commit(self, *args, **kwargs):
        return super().create_commit(*args, **{**kwargs, "num_threads": 1})


def publication_target(api, repo_id, files, download=hf_hub_download):
    """Require an owned public destination; replace only manifest-managed paths."""
    owner, separator, name = repo_id.partition("/")
    if not separator or not name or "/" in name or api.whoami()["name"] != owner:
        raise ValueError("Release destination must be in the authenticated user's namespace")
    try:
        info = api.repo_info(repo_id, repo_type="dataset")
    except RepositoryNotFoundError:
        return None, []
    if info.private is not False:
        raise ValueError("Release destination must be public")
    head = info.sha
    try:
        old = json.loads(
            Path(
                download(repo_id, "release-files.json", repo_type="dataset", revision=head)
            ).read_text()
        )
    except EntryNotFoundError:
        if set(api.list_repo_files(repo_id, repo_type="dataset", revision=head)) - {
            ".gitattributes"
        }:
            raise ValueError("Existing destination has no managed release manifest") from None
        return head, []
    if old["repo_id"] != repo_id:
        raise ValueError("Previous manifest belongs to another destination")
    obsolete = sorted(set(old["files"]) - set(files["files"]))
    if any(
        p.startswith("/") or ".." in Path(p).parts or any(char in p for char in "*?[")
        for p in obsolete
    ):
        raise ValueError("Unsafe managed path in previous release manifest")
    return head, obsolete


def main():
    staged, receipt = map(Path, sys.argv[1:])
    files = verify_release(staged)
    repo_id = files["repo_id"]
    api = SerialHfApi()
    head, obsolete = publication_target(api, repo_id, files)

    class Replacement:
        def __init__(self):
            self.parent_commit = head

        def create_repo(self, *args, **kwargs):
            return api.create_repo(*args, **kwargs)

        def upload_folder(self, **kwargs):
            assert kwargs["repo_id"] == repo_id
            commit = api.upload_folder(
                **kwargs,
                parent_commit=self.parent_commit,
                delete_patterns=obsolete or None,
            )
            self.parent_commit = commit.oid
            return commit

        def upload_file(self, **kwargs):
            assert kwargs["repo_id"] == repo_id
            commit = api.upload_file(**kwargs, parent_commit=self.parent_commit)
            self.parent_commit = commit.oid
            return commit

        def __getattr__(self, key):
            return getattr(api, key)

    result = publish_release(staged, api=Replacement(), receipt=receipt)
    print(json.dumps(result))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Verify a pinned upstream release after downloading its mode-preserving archive."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import gzip
import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
import tarfile
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path, PurePosixPath

from repo2rlenv.campaigns.release import verify_release
from repo2rlenv.emitter.bundle import inspect_bundle

MAX_FILE_BYTES = 64 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 256 * 1024 * 1024
MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS = 4096
MAX_METADATA_BYTES = 16384
MAX_PATH_BYTES = 1024


def safe_path(name: str) -> Path:
    if not name or len(name.encode()) > MAX_PATH_BYTES or "\\" in name or "\x00" in name:
        raise ValueError("Unsafe release path")
    value = PurePosixPath(name)
    if value.is_absolute() or ".." in value.parts or value.as_posix() != name:
        raise ValueError("Unsafe release path")
    return Path(name)


def digest(path: Path) -> str:
    result = hashlib.sha256()
    with path.open("rb") as stream:
        while chunk := stream.read(1024 * 1024):
            result.update(chunk)
    return result.hexdigest()


def bounded_archive(source, destination, entries):
    """Bound raw headers before tarfile parses extended metadata; validate before extracting."""
    expected_files = {name for name in entries if name.startswith("tasks/")}
    expected_dirs = {
        parent.as_posix()
        for name in expected_files
        for parent in Path(name).parents
        if parent != Path(".")
    }
    with tempfile.TemporaryFile() as raw:
        with gzip.open(source, "rb") as compressed:
            total = 0
            for index in range(MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS + 1):
                header = compressed.read(512)
                if header == b"\0" * 512:
                    raw.write(header)
                    break
                if len(header) != 512 or index == MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS:
                    raise ValueError("Invalid or excessive archive headers")
                member = tarfile.TarInfo.frombuf(header, "utf-8", "surrogateescape")
                if member.size < 0 or member.size > MAX_FILE_BYTES:
                    raise ValueError("Archive member exceeds size bound")
                if (
                    member.type
                    in {
                        tarfile.XHDTYPE,
                        tarfile.XGLTYPE,
                        tarfile.GNUTYPE_LONGNAME,
                        tarfile.GNUTYPE_LONGLINK,
                    }
                    and member.size > MAX_METADATA_BYTES
                ):
                    raise ValueError("Archive metadata exceeds bound")
                size = (member.size + 511) // 512 * 512
                total += 512 + size
                if total > MAX_TOTAL_BYTES + 8 * 1024 * 1024:
                    raise ValueError("Archive expansion exceeds bound")
                raw.write(header)
                while size:
                    block = compressed.read(min(size, 65536))
                    if not block:
                        raise ValueError("Truncated archive")
                    raw.write(block)
                    size -= len(block)
        seen = set()
        raw.seek(0)
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=raw, mode="r|") as archive:
            for member in archive:
                if member.name in seen or len(seen) >= MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS:
                    raise ValueError("Duplicate or excessive archive entries")
                seen.add(member.name)
                safe_path(member.name)
                if member.isdir():
                    if member.name not in expected_dirs:
                        raise ValueError("Unexpected archive directory")
                elif member.isfile() and not member.sparse:
                    entry = entries.get(member.name)
                    if (
                        member.name not in expected_files
                        or member.size != entry["bytes"]
                        or member.mode != entry["mode"]
                    ):
                        raise ValueError("Archive differs from release manifest")
                else:
                    raise ValueError("Archive must contain regular files and directories")
        if not expected_files.issubset(seen):
            raise ValueError("Missing archive files")
        raw.seek(0)
        with tarfile.open(fileobj=raw, mode="r|") as archive:
            for member in archive:
                if member.isfile():
                    target = destination / safe_path(member.name)
                    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                    with archive.extractfile(member) as src, target.open("xb") as dst:
                        shutil.copyfileobj(src, dst, length=65536)
                    target.chmod(member.mode)


def check_download(repo_id: str, revision: str, destination: Path, download) -> dict:
    """Download only public release files, restore modes, then call upstream checks.

    ``download(name)`` must fetch from the explicit immutable publication revision.
    A new destination prevents cached local task files from satisfying the check.
    """
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{40}", revision):
        raise ValueError("Use the immutable publication commit")
    destination.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    manifest_source = Path(download("release-files.json"))
    if manifest_source.stat().st_size > 1024 * 1024:
        raise ValueError("Release manifest is too large")
    manifest = json.loads(manifest_source.read_text())
    if manifest["repo_id"] != repo_id:
        raise ValueError("Downloaded release belongs to a different repository")
    entries = manifest["files"]
    if sum(v["bytes"] for v in entries.values()) > MAX_TOTAL_BYTES:
        raise ValueError("Release exceeds the bounded local download allowance")
    for name, entry in entries.items():
        safe_path(name)
        if not 0 <= entry["bytes"] <= MAX_FILE_BYTES or not 0 <= entry["mode"] <= 0o777:
            raise ValueError("Invalid release size or mode")
    shutil.copyfile(manifest_source, destination / "release-files.json")
    for name, entry in entries.items():
        if name.startswith("tasks/"):
            continue
        source = Path(download(name))
        if source.stat().st_size != entry["bytes"] or digest(source) != entry["sha256"]:
            raise ValueError(f"Downloaded bytes changed: {name}")
        target = destination / safe_path(name)
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        shutil.copyfile(source, target)
        target.chmod(entry["mode"])
    bounded_archive(destination / "tasks.tar.gz", destination, entries)
    verify_release(destination)
    release = json.loads((destination / "manifest.json").read_text())
    bundles = []
    for row in release["tasks"]:
        identity = inspect_bundle(destination / safe_path(row["path"]))
        if not identity["integrity_passed"] or identity["bundle_hash"] != row["bundle_hash"]:
            raise ValueError("Downloaded task identity changed")
        bundles.append({"task_id": row["task_id"], "bundle_hash": identity["bundle_hash"]})
    return {"repo_id": repo_id, "revision": revision, "verified": True, "tasks": bundles}


def main():
    from huggingface_hub import hf_hub_download

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("repo_id")
    parser.add_argument("revision")
    parser.add_argument("destination", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--receipt", type=Path, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    result = check_download(
        args.repo_id,
        args.revision,
        args.destination,
        lambda name: hf_hub_download(
            args.repo_id, name, repo_type="dataset", revision=args.revision, force_download=True
        ),
    )
    args.receipt.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2) + "\n")
    print(json.dumps(result))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Both terminal artifacts are retained: the HMMER3 profile and domain-search table. Eighteen final controls behaved as expected; native oracle/no-op rewards were 1/0 and the blind GLM solver scored 1. The known unused packaged answer fixture was removed and the native build enforces the same exclusion. No operator edited the scientific task.       "name": "val-repr-permitted-freedoms",
      "rationale": "Representation control exercising only the freedoms the public contract explicitly grants: (a) column alignment/trailing whitespace in LuxC.hmm is not compared \u2014 reserialize each numeric row with single-space separation (leading indent preserved) and print each 5-decimal value with an extra trailing zero (2.07294 -> 2.072940, identical value); (b) HMM numeric tolerance 2e-5 \u2014 deviate EFFN (1.989990 -> 1.990000) and all three STATS LOCAL lambda/mu values by exactly 1e-5 (half the tolerance); (c) LuxC.domtbl comment header lines are ignored \u2014 insert one; (d) domtbl tolerances \u2014 deviate the first row's full-sequence score by 0.05 (<=0.06), its full-sequence/c-/i-E-values by ~4.3-4.8% relative (<=5%) and its acc by 0.005 (<=0.006), and spell an E-value with an explicit mantissa (2.1e-169 vs 2e-169). Every changed value stays strictly inside the published tolerance bounds, so all checks must pass. The dominant application-relevant use of these tolerances is the fixed-width decimal serialization of HMMER values; this probe does not attempt any recomputation.",
      "script": "# Valid representation alternative. Exercise ONLY freedoms the public contract\n# explicitly grants:\n#  (a) LuxC.hmm: \"Trailing whitespace and column alignment is not compared\" --\n#      re-emit the COMPO and per-position rows with single-space separation\n#      (leading indent preserved), and reserialize each 5-decimal number with\n#      an additional trailing zero (identical value, wider print).\n#  (b) LuxC.hmm: numeric parameters have absolute tolerance 2e-5 -- deviate\n#      EFFN and the STATS LOCAL calibration values by 1e-5 (half tolerance).\n#  (c) LuxC.domtbl: comment header lines are ignored -- insert one.\n#  (d) LuxC.domtbl: score tolerance 0.06, E-value relative tolerance 5%,\n#      acc tolerance 0.006 -- deviate one row strictly inside each bound, and\n#      spell an E-value with an explicit mantissa (2.0e-169 style vs 2e-169).\nimport re\n\n# ---------- LuxC.hmm ----------\np = \"LuxC.hmm\"\nlines = open(p).read().split(\"\\n\")\nout = []\nmode = 0  # 0 header, 1 after HMM header, 2 blocks\nfor ln in lines:\n    if ln.startswith(\"EFFN \"):\n        assert ln.split()[1] == \"1.989990\"\n        out.append(\"EFFN  1.990000\")          # |diff| = 1e-5 <= 2e-5\n        continue\n    if ln.startswith(\"STATS LOCAL\"):\n        f = ln.split()\n        lam = float(f[3]) + 0.00001             # |diff| = 1e-5 <= 2e-5\n        mu = float(f[4]) + 0.00001\n        out.append(\" \".join(f[:3]) + \" \" + (\"%8.4f %8.5f\" % (lam, mu)))\n        continue\n    if mode == 0 and ln.startswith(\"HMM \"):\n        mode = 1\n        out.append(ln)\n        continue\n    if mode == 1 and ln.lstrip().startswith(\"m->m\"):\n        mode = 2\n        out.append(ln)\n        continue\n    if mode == 2 and ln.strip() and not ln.startswith(\"//\"):\n        lead = ln[: len(ln) - len(ln.lstrip())]  # keep leading indent exactly\n        toks = ln.split()\n        new = []\n        for t in toks:\n            if t == \"*\":\n                new.append(t)\n            elif re.fullmatch(r\"\\d+\\.\\d+\", t):\n                new.append(t + \"0\")              # same value, wider print\n            else:\n                new.append(t)\n        out.append(lead + \" \".join(new))\n        continue\n    out.append(ln)\nopen(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(out))\n\n# ---------- LuxC.domtbl ----------\np = \"LuxC.domtbl\"\nlines = open(p).read().split(\"\\n\")\ndi = [i for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.strip() and not ln.startswith(\"#\")]\nassert di and lines[di[0]].startswith(\"tr|B6ESM7|\")\nf = lines[di[0]].split(None, 22)\nassert f[6] == \"2e-169\" and f[7] == \"553.3\" and f[11] == \"2.3e-169\" \\\n    and f[12] == \"2.3e-169\" and f[21] == \"0.99\"\nf[6] = \"2.1e-169\"    # ~4.76% <= 5% relative, also explicit-mantissa spelling\nf[7] = \"553.25\"      # |diff| = 0.05 <= 0.06\nf[11] = \"2.2e-169\"   # ~4.35% <= 5%\nf[12] = \"2.4e-169\"   # ~4.35% <= 5%\nf[21] = \"0.985\"      # |diff| = 0.005 <= 0.006\nlines[di[0]] = \" \".join(f)\nlines.insert(0, \"# representation variation - comment lines are ignored\")\nopen(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(lines))\nprint(\"done\")\n"
    }

        },

          "quote": "      1   2.07294  4.36058  3.81125  2.93462  3.48431  3.76914  4.04102  2.43908  3.16681  1.75164  3.46932  3.15811  4.14526  3.45003  3.09626  3.02978  2.97564  2.15870  4.95927  3.74369      1 l - - -"

      "name": "w-hmm-tolerance-boundary",
      "rationale": "Deviation just beyond the 2e-5 absolute HMM tolerance, applied to three different kinds of compared values: EFFN 1.989990 -> 1.990013 (2.3e-5 off), a STATS LOCAL MSV lambda/mu pair by 3e-5, and the position-1 match emission 2.07294 -> 2.07297 (3e-5). Everything else is identical. This probes the acceptance boundary for exactly-serialized values rather than a large error, verifying the grader's absolute-tolerance rule rejects deviations that exceed half of one printed decimal unit.",
      "script": "# Tolerance-boundary wrong result in the profile HMM: deviate EFFN, one STATS\n# parameter and a single position-1 emission value by just beyond the 2e-5\n# absolute tolerance.\np = \"LuxC.hmm\"\nlines = open(p).read().split(\"\\n\")\nseen = 0\nfor i, ln in enumerate(lines):\n    if ln.startswith(\"EFFN \"):\n        assert ln.split()[1] == \"1.989990\"\n        lines[i] = \"EFFN  1.990013\"            # diff 2.3e-5 > 2e-5\n        seen += 1\n    elif ln.startswith(\"STATS LOCAL MSV\"):\n        f = ln.split()\n        lines[i] = \" \".join(f[:3]) + \" \" + (\"%8.5f %8.5f\" % (float(f[3]) - 0.00003, float(f[4]) + 0.00003))\n        seen += 1\n    elif seen >= 2 and ln.startswith(\"      1 \"):\n        toks = ln.split()\n        assert toks[0] == \"1\" and toks[1] == \"2.07294\"\n        toks[1] = \"2.07297\"                    # diff 3e-5 > 2e-5\n        lines[i] = \"      \" + \"  \".join(toks)\n        seen += 1\n        break\nassert seen == 3, seen\nopen(p, \"w\").write(\"\\n\".join(lines))\nprint(\"ok\")\n"
